Sourced from the World Bank indicator NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG.

indicators.title: CPI inflation
indicators.subtitle: Consumer prices
indicators.details:
Consumer price inflation tracks the annual change in the cost of a representative basket of goods and services. It is a broad measure of household purchasing-power pressure.

The series is useful alongside growth, exchange-rate, and trade indicators because imported costs and domestic demand can move inflation in different directions. Values are annual and come through the World Bank open API.

indicators.title: Per capita Net National Income
indicators.subtitle: Per capita NNI at current prices in Indian Rupees
indicators.details:
Per capita Net National Income (NNI) measures national income divided by population in current Indian Rupees. It expanded from ₹63,462 in FY2012 to ₹2.18 Lakh in FY2026.

Sourced from MOSPI National Accounts Statistics and official Economic Survey statements.

series.source: MOSPI National Accounts Statistics & Economic Survey (Per Capita Net National Income - NNI at Current Prices in INR)

indicators.title: Per capita GNI in PPP dollars
indicators.subtitle: GNI per capita in Purchasing Power Parity current international $
indicators.details:
GNI per capita converted to international dollars using purchasing power parity (PPP) rates, accounting for domestic price differences.

Sourced from World Bank Open Data indicator NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD.

datasets.label: Per capita GNI in PPP dollars

series.source: World Bank Open Data NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD (GNI per capita, PPP in current international $)

indicators.title: GST collections
indicators.subtitle: Gross monthly GST revenue
indicators.details:
GST collections are a high-frequency signal of recorded consumption and production moving through India's indirect-tax system. Strong receipts can reflect higher activity, improved compliance, price effects, or a combination of these factors.

The monthly series is collated from the Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.1. It should not be confused with a forecast or an estimate.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Fiscal deficit
indicators.subtitle: Union fiscal deficit as share of GDP
indicators.details:
The fiscal deficit is the gap between government expenditure and receipts excluding borrowings. It indicates how much the public sector needs to finance during a fiscal year.

The annual series is collated from official Economic Survey table 2.4 Excel files across previous editions and reported as a share of GDP.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 2.4; fiscal deficit as percent of GDP

indicators.title: Bank credit
indicators.subtitle: Domestic credit to private sector
indicators.details:
Domestic credit to the private sector measures financial-sector lending relative to the size of the economy. It can signal whether businesses and households have expanding or tightening access to finance.

Credit growth is not automatically positive: the composition, repayment quality, and cost of borrowing matter. This annual ratio is a structural indicator, not a substitute for RBI monthly banking statistics.

indicators.title: GDP per capita
indicators.subtitle: Current US dollars per person
indicators.details:
GDP per capita divides the value of economic output by population. It is a broad scale indicator for comparing the economy over time, but it does not describe inequality, household income, or quality of life by itself.

The current-dollar series is sensitive to exchange rates and inflation. Read it alongside real growth and purchasing-power measures for a more complete picture.

indicators.title: Current account balance
indicators.subtitle: Balance as share of GDP
indicators.details:
The current account records trade in goods and services, income flows, and transfers with the rest of the world. A deficit means the country is spending more foreign exchange on these flows than it receives during the period.

This indicator connects directly to reserves, the rupee, and external financing conditions. It is shown as a share of GDP to make changes in national scale easier to compare.

indicators.title: Broad money
indicators.subtitle: Money supply as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Broad money captures currency and deposits available across the financial system. Relative to GDP, it provides a long-run view of liquidity and financial deepening.

It is not a direct measure of inflation or spending. Credit conditions, velocity, policy rates, and the distribution of deposits all influence how money supply affects the economy.

indicators.title: Tax revenue
indicators.subtitle: Tax revenue as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Tax revenue shows how much public revenue is collected through taxes relative to the size of the economy. It helps put fiscal capacity and public-service financing in a longer-run context.

The ratio can change because collections move, GDP moves, or both. It does not identify tax burden distribution or distinguish every type of levy.

indicators.title: Government consumption
indicators.subtitle: General government final consumption
indicators.details:
Government final consumption measures public-sector spending on goods and services relative to GDP. It is a useful context signal for the size of direct government demand in the economy.

This is not the same as the fiscal deficit: transfers, capital spending, receipts, and borrowing are treated differently in national accounts.

indicators.title: Foreign direct investment
indicators.subtitle: Net FDI inflows as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Foreign direct investment captures net cross-border investment intended to establish a lasting interest in an enterprise. Relative to GDP, it shows how important foreign investment flows are compared with national output.

A single year can be volatile because of large transactions, restructurings, or exceptional deals. It should be read with the current account and reserves.

indicators.title: Domestic savings
indicators.subtitle: Gross domestic savings as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Gross domestic savings is the portion of national output not used for final consumption. It provides a macro view of the resources potentially available for domestic investment.

The indicator does not show which households, firms, or public institutions save, nor whether savings are invested productively. Its value is strongest when compared with investment and external financing.

indicators.title: Real household consumption per capita
indicators.subtitle: Household final consumption per person, constant 2015 US dollars
indicators.details:
Households and non-profit institutions serving households (NPISHs) final consumption expenditure per capita, expressed in constant 2015 US dollars. It provides a long-run, inflation-adjusted signal of material consumption per person.

It is an average, not a measure of distribution or each household's purchasing power, and it does not capture unpaid work or public services. Sourced from World Bank indicator NE.CON.PRVT.PC.KD.

indicators.title: GDP at Purchasing Power Parity
indicators.subtitle: Gross domestic product in current international dollars
indicators.details: GDP converted using purchasing-power-parity rates for cross-country price differences. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: GDP Deflator Inflation
indicators.subtitle: Annual GDP deflator inflation
indicators.details: Annual change in the GDP deflator, covering prices across domestically produced output. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Gross Capital Formation
indicators.subtitle: Gross capital formation as a share of GDP
indicators.details: Investment in fixed assets and changes in inventories as a share of GDP. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Household Consumption Share
indicators.subtitle: Household consumption expenditure as a share of GDP
indicators.details: Household and nonprofit institution final consumption expenditure as a share of GDP. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Gross Savings Rate
indicators.subtitle: Gross savings as a share of GDP
indicators.details: Gross national savings as a share of GDP. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Central Government Debt
indicators.subtitle: Central government debt as a share of GDP
indicators.details: Central government debt relative to GDP. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: GDP Sector Composition
indicators.subtitle: Latest reported agriculture, industry and services shares of GDP
indicators.details: A doughnut view of the latest common World Bank sectoral value-added shares. Other GDP components are explicitly shown as the residual to 100%, not as a directly reported sector.

series.note: Value-added shares for the latest common World Bank observation (2025). Other GDP components are the residual to 100%, including net product taxes and rounding differences; this is not a directly reported sector.
series.source: World Bank API NV.AGR.TOTL.ZS; World Bank API NV.IND.TOTL.ZS; World Bank API NV.SRV.TOTL.ZS

indicators.title: Bank Lending Interest Rate
indicators.subtitle: Average commercial-bank lending rate
indicators.details: Average commercial-bank lending rate. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator FR.INR.LEND); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: Average commercial-bank lending rate. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator FR.INR.LEND); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Real Interest Rate
indicators.subtitle: Lending rate adjusted for GDP-deflator inflation
indicators.details: Lending rate adjusted for GDP-deflator inflation. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator FR.INR.RINR); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: Lending rate adjusted for GDP-deflator inflation. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator FR.INR.RINR); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: GDP by Expenditure (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Share of GDP
indicators.details: Share of GDP, latest year with every component reported (2025). World Bank indicators NE.CON.PRVT.ZS, NE.CON.GOVT.ZS, NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS. 'Net exports & inventories' is the residual to 100%, not a directly reported category.

series.note: Share of GDP, latest year with every component reported (2025). World Bank indicators NE.CON.PRVT.ZS, NE.CON.GOVT.ZS, NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS. 'Net exports & inventories' is the residual to 100%, not a directly reported category.
series.source: World Bank API NE.CON.PRVT.ZS, NE.CON.GOVT.ZS, NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS

indicators.title: Rupee exchange rate
indicators.subtitle: INR per US dollar
indicators.details:
This series expresses the Indian rupee required to purchase one US dollar. A rising value means rupee depreciation against the dollar, all else equal.

Monthly exchange-rate observations are collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.4, with RBI DBIE linked as the official portal.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Trade share of GDP
indicators.subtitle: Exports plus imports as share of GDP
indicators.details:
Trade openness compares the combined value of exports and imports with GDP. It gives context for how strongly India's output is connected to external demand, imported inputs, and global price movements.

This is a ratio rather than a rupee total, so it can rise because trade grows or because GDP changes. The series is sourced through the World Bank open API.

indicators.title: Foreign exchange reserves
indicators.subtitle: Total reserves including gold
indicators.details:
Foreign-exchange reserves are external assets held by the monetary authority, including gold in this indicator. They help provide resilience against external-payment stress and exchange-rate volatility.

Reserve adequacy should be read with imports, debt, and the current account rather than treated as a standalone score. The displayed series is annual and denominated in current US dollars.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise exports
indicators.subtitle: Goods exports
indicators.details:
Merchandise exports measure the value of goods sold abroad. They connect the dashboard to external demand, foreign exchange earnings, and manufacturing competitiveness.

The monthly values are collated from Economic Survey table 9.4 and should be interpreted with imports and the current account.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise imports
indicators.subtitle: Goods imports
indicators.details:
Merchandise imports measure the value of goods purchased from abroad. They capture domestic demand, imported inputs, energy exposure, and pressure on the trade balance.

The monthly values are collated from Economic Survey table 9.4 and are not the same as total services-inclusive imports.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Merchandise trade balance
indicators.subtitle: Goods exports minus goods imports
indicators.details:
The monthly merchandise trade balance is calculated as goods exports minus goods imports. Positive values indicate a surplus and negative values a deficit.

This national total excludes services and does not identify balances with individual countries or regions.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.4; calculated as merchandise exports minus merchandise imports (national balance, not partner-specific)

indicators.title: Merchandise balance by trading partner
indicators.subtitle: Exports minus imports for leading partners
indicators.details:
This chart compares India's reported merchandise exports and imports with its leading trading partners for the latest year with matching observations. Positive values indicate a surplus; negative values indicate a deficit.

UN Comtrade reports exports on an FOB basis and imports on a CIF basis, so values are not perfectly symmetric. The chart covers goods only, not services, and is limited to the leading partners with verified code mappings.

series.source: UN Comtrade API, India merchandise trade by partner (2025); exports FOB minus imports CIF, top partners by trade value

indicators.title: Exports of Goods and Services
indicators.subtitle: Exports of goods and services as a share of GDP
indicators.details: Exports of goods and services relative to GDP. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Imports of Goods and Services
indicators.subtitle: Imports of goods and services as a share of GDP

indicators.title: ICT Service Exports
indicators.subtitle: Computer, communications and other services, % of service exports
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of India's service exports that come from IT, software, communications and related business services.

How to read it — A high, rising share shows how central the IT and global-capability-centre industry is to India's exports.

Why it matters — Services exports pay for much of India's merchandise trade deficit, making this sector a pillar of external stability.

series.note: Computer, communications and other services, % of service exports. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: External Debt Stocks
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total external debt owed to non-residents as a share of gross national income. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 18.58% of GNI in 2024. Lower means the country's foreign obligations are small relative to its income.

Why it matters — A modest ratio protects against currency and rollover crises.

series.note: External Debt Stocks: India's annual series, 1980 to 2024; the latest value is 18.58% of GNI. Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: External Debt Stocks: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total external debt owed to non-residents as a share of gross national income. This chart overlays India with 3 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, Brazil, Bangladesh. Lower means the country's foreign obligations are small relative to its income.

Why it matters — A modest ratio protects against currency and rollover crises.

series.note: External Debt Stocks: India against 3 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: External Debt Stocks: Peer Ranking (2024)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total external debt owed to non-residents as a share of gross national income. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2024; India ranks 8 of 9 (1 = highest value). Lower means the country's foreign obligations are small relative to its income.

Why it matters — A modest ratio protects against currency and rollover crises.

series.note: External Debt Stocks, 2024: India ranks 8 of 9 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: External Debt Stock
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total outstanding external debt (public, publicly guaranteed and private) in US dollars. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 716.46 USD bn in 2024. The line shows how fast India's dollar obligations have grown.

Why it matters — The absolute stock matters because servicing it drains foreign-exchange reserves.

series.note: External Debt Stock: India's annual series, 1980 to 2024; the latest value is 716.46 USD bn. Source: World Bank API DT.DOD.DECT.CD (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Debt Service
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Principal plus interest paid on external debt as a share of exports of goods, services and income. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 10.49% of exports in 2024. A rising line means a bigger slice of export earnings is spent on debt.

Why it matters — Debt service relative to export earnings is a classic stress gauge for external solvency.

series.note: Debt Service: India's annual series, 1980 to 2024; the latest value is 10.49% of exports. Source: World Bank API DT.TDS.DECT.EX.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Debt Service: Decade Averages
indicators.subtitle: India, average per decade
indicators.details:
What it shows — Principal plus interest paid on external debt as a share of exports of goods, services and income. Annual values are averaged within each decade to smooth year-to-year noise.

How to read it — Compare bars left to right: the 2020s average is 10.36% of exports against 23.58% of exports in the 1980s. A rising line means a bigger slice of export earnings is spent on debt.

Why it matters — Debt service relative to export earnings is a classic stress gauge for external solvency.

series.note: Debt Service: decade averages for India; the 2020s average is -13.22% of exports below the 1980s. Source: World Bank API DT.TDS.DECT.EX.ZS (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Foreign-Exchange Reserves: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total reserves including gold held by the central bank, in US dollars. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 4 of 13 (1 = highest value). Bigger slices or bars mean a larger buffer for defending the currency and paying for imports.

Why it matters — Reserves are the first line of defence against capital-flow shocks.

series.note: Foreign-Exchange Reserves, 2025: India ranks 4 of 13 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API FI.RES.TOTL.CD (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Foreign-Exchange Reserves: Share Among Peers (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Each country's share of the 15-country total
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total reserves including gold held by the central bank, in US dollars. Slices show each country's share of the sampled countries' total.

How to read it — Slices are shares of the group total in 2025; India holds 7.7% and ranks 4 of 13. A bigger slice means a larger absolute amount, not a better outcome.

Why it matters — Reserves are the first line of defence against capital-flow shocks.

series.note: Foreign-Exchange Reserves, 2025: India holds 7.7% of the group total and ranks 4 of 13. Source: World Bank API FI.RES.TOTL.CD (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Remittances Received
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Personal transfers and compensation of employees sent home by workers abroad, in US dollars. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 150.71 USD bn in 2025. A rising line means more foreign income flowing to households.

Why it matters — India is the world's largest remittance recipient, a stable source of foreign currency.

series.note: Remittances Received: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 150.71 USD bn. Source: World Bank API BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Personal transfers and compensation of employees sent home by workers abroad, in US dollars. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 1 of 15 (1 = highest value). A rising line means more foreign income flowing to households.

Why it matters — India is the world's largest remittance recipient, a stable source of foreign currency.

series.note: Remittances Received, 2025: India ranks 1 of 15 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API BX.TRF.PWKR.CD.DT (World Bank International Debt Statistics / IMF); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.subtitle: Each country's share of the 15-country total
indicators.details:
What it shows — Personal transfers and compensation of employees sent home by workers abroad, in US dollars. Slices show each country's share of the sampled countries' total.

How to read it — Slices are shares of the group total in 2025; India holds 38.6% and ranks 1 of 15. A bigger slice means a larger absolute amount, not a better outcome.

indicators.title: NITI Export Preparedness Index: overall score by state and UT
indicators.subtitle: EPI 2022 overall score out of 100
indicators.details:
What it shows — How prepared each state and UT is to export, scored across policy, business ecosystem, export ecosystem and export performance.

How to read it — Tamil Nadu (80.89), Maharashtra, Karnataka and Gujarat lead; Himalayan states and small UTs trail.

Why it matters — Exports depend on state-level logistics, policy and industry, so state scores show where capacity is missing.

indicators.title: Indian crude oil basket
indicators.subtitle: Average crude oil price
indicators.details:
The Indian crude oil basket price tracks an indicative average of crude prices relevant to India's import exposure. It helps explain fuel-cost pressure, inflation risk, and the external trade bill.

This is a crude price indicator, not a retail petrol or diesel price index. It is collated from Economic Survey table 9.3.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Fuel consumption
indicators.subtitle: Petroleum product consumption
indicators.details:
Fuel consumption measures petroleum product demand and is a useful activity proxy for transport, industry, and household energy use.

It is not a fuel price index. The dashboard labels it explicitly as consumption and sources it from Economic Survey table 9.4.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Indian market indices
indicators.subtitle: Sensex, Nifty, and Nifty VIX; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This combined graph compares India's major equity-market indices and volatility using one normalized base-100 view. It makes direction and relative movement readable despite the different scales of the Sensex, Nifty, and VIX.

The monthly observations are collated from Economic Survey table 9.3. This is a market-context dashboard, not investment advice, and rebasing means the plotted values are relative rather than index levels.

series.source: BSE and NSE index histories, rebased to 100

indicators.title: Global equity market comparison
indicators.subtitle: BSE Sensex vs S&P 500, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, and Shanghai Composite; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This graph compares India's primary equity benchmark (BSE Sensex) against leading global market indices (S&P 500, FTSE 100, Nikkei 225, Shanghai Composite) rebased to 100.

It illustrates the long-run compounding and relative performance of Indian capital markets alongside the world's major financial hubs.

series.source: BSE India, S&P Dow Jones, FTSE Russell, Nikkei Inc., SSE; Base 100 = 2000

indicators.title: World top economies GDP comparison
indicators.subtitle: GDP trajectories of India, US, China, Germany, Japan, and UK
indicators.details:
This chart plots the gross domestic product of India alongside the world's largest economies (United States, China, Germany, Japan, and United Kingdom) in current US dollars.

It contextualizes India's rise from an emerging developing economy following independence to one of the world's top 5 economic powerhouses.

series.source: World Bank API NY.GDP.MKTP.CD (GDP in current USD Trillion)

indicators.title: India sectoral market engines
indicators.subtitle: Nifty IT, Nifty Bank, Nifty Auto, Nifty Energy, and Sensex; rebased to 100
indicators.details:
This series tracks key sectoral engines of India's stock market expansion—Technology, Banking & Financials, Automotive, and Energy—rebased to 100 alongside the benchmark Sensex.

It reveals how different industry pillars have spearheaded growth across economic cycles.

indicators.title: Global inflation benchmark comparison
indicators.subtitle: Consumer price inflation in India, US, and Euro Area
indicators.details:
This indicator compares consumer price inflation rate trends across India, the United States, and the Euro Area.

Reading India's inflation alongside major global central bank economies highlights how global commodity shocks, monetary policy, and exchange rates impact domestic price stability.

series.source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (Annual CPI inflation %)

indicators.title: Consumer Price Index (2010 = 100)
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — The consumer price index tracks the cost of a typical household basket, rebased so 2010 equals 100. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 233.06 index in 2025. A steeper line means faster cumulative price rises since the 2010 base.

Why it matters — The index level shows how much purchasing power has been eroded over the long run.

series.note: Consumer Price Index (2010 = 100): India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 233.06 index. Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 7 of 14 (1 = highest value). A steeper line means faster cumulative price rises since the 2010 base.

Why it matters — The index level shows how much purchasing power has been eroded over the long run.

series.note: Consumer Price Index (2010 = 100), 2025: India ranks 7 of 14 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Consumer Price Inflation: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual percentage change in consumer prices. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Spikes show inflation episodes; a line near zero or below shows stable or falling prices.

Why it matters — Inflation decides real incomes, interest rates and central-bank policy.

series.note: Consumer Price Inflation: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 9 of 14 (1 = highest value). Spikes show inflation episodes; a line near zero or below shows stable or falling prices.

Why it matters — Inflation decides real incomes, interest rates and central-bank policy.

series.note: Consumer Price Inflation, 2025: India ranks 9 of 14 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

Why it matters — Inflation decides real incomes, interest rates and central-bank policy.

indicators.title: PPP Conversion Factor
indicators.subtitle: India, 1990-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — How many rupees are needed to buy what one international dollar buys in the United States. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 20.09 LCU per int. $ in 2025. A rising line means the rupee's domestic purchasing power is falling relative to the dollar's.

Why it matters — It is the basis for converting India's GDP into internationally comparable PPP terms.

series.note: PPP Conversion Factor: India's annual series, 1990 to 2025; the latest value is 20.09 LCU per int. $. Source: World Bank API PA.NUS.PPP (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Comparative Price Level of Consumption: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Private-consumption PPP divided by the market exchange rate; values below 1 mean prices are lower than in the US. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Lower bars mean everyday goods and services are cheaper in dollar terms.

Why it matters — A low price level helps household affordability but also depresses dollar-measured GDP.

series.note: Comparative Price Level of Consumption: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, PA.NUS.FCRF (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Broad Money Growth
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2021
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual growth in broad money (M3), the stock of currency, deposits and near-money. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 11.3% in 2021. Faster growth than GDP often precedes higher inflation or credit booms.

Why it matters — Money supply growth is a leading indicator for inflation and financial-sector expansion.

series.note: Broad Money Growth: India's annual series, 1980 to 2021; the latest value is 11.3%. Source: World Bank API FM.LBL.BMNY.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2021.

How to read it — Compare bars left to right: the 2020s average is 11.89% against 17.06% in the 1980s. Faster growth than GDP often precedes higher inflation or credit booms.

Why it matters — Money supply growth is a leading indicator for inflation and financial-sector expansion.

series.note: Broad Money Growth: decade averages for India; the 2020s average is -5.17% below the 1980s. Source: World Bank API FM.LBL.BMNY.ZG (IMF / World Bank price statistics); latest year with data: 2021.

indicators.title: Gross Capital Formation
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross capital formation is the share of GDP spent on new fixed assets and inventory build-up. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 34.6% in 2025. A higher share means the economy is channelling more output into future capacity.

Why it matters — Investment is the engine of medium-term growth; India's rate shows how much of its growth is capital-led.

series.note: Gross Capital Formation: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 34.6%. Source: World Bank API NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: GNI per Capita (PPP)
indicators.subtitle: India, 1990-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross national income per person converted at purchasing-power-parity so prices are comparable across countries. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 11,600 int. $ in 2025. Higher means more income per resident after adjusting for local price levels.

Why it matters — PPP income shows real living standards better than market exchange rates do.

series.note: GNI per Capita (PPP): India's annual series, 1990 to 2025; the latest value is 11,600 int. $. Source: World Bank API NY.GNP.PCAP.PP.CD (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Lines above India mean peers save more of their income.

Why it matters — High domestic savings let a country fund investment without relying on foreign capital.

series.note: Gross Savings Rate: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API NY.GNS.ICTR.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: External Balance on Goods & Services
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — The external balance is exports minus imports of goods and services as a share of GDP. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at -1.74% in 2025. Values below zero are trade deficits; above zero are surpluses.

Why it matters — A persistent deficit must be financed by foreign inflows, so it signals external vulnerability.

series.note: External Balance on Goods & Services: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is -1.74%. Source: World Bank API NE.RSB.GNFS.ZS (IMF / World Bank national accounts); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Women with a Financial Account
indicators.subtitle: India, 2011-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of adult women owning an account at a bank, other financial institution or mobile-money provider. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 89.25% of women 15+ in 2024. Points rise survey by survey; the gap to the 100% mark is the unbanked women's share.

Why it matters — Women's account ownership is the base on which digital credit and payments can scale.

series.note: Women with a Financial Account: India's annual series, 2011 to 2024; the latest value is 89.25% of women 15+. Source: World Bank API FX.OWN.TOTL.FE.ZS (World Bank Global Findex / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2024

What it shows — Share of adult women owning an account at a bank, other financial institution or mobile-money provider. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2024; India ranks 6 of 15 (1 = highest value). Points rise survey by survey; the gap to the 100% mark is the unbanked women's share.

Why it matters — Women's account ownership is the base on which digital credit and payments can scale.

indicators.title: Poorest 40% with an Account
indicators.subtitle: India, 2011-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Account ownership among adults in the poorest 40% of households. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 86.32% in 2024. Higher means formal finance is reaching low-income households.

Why it matters — Inclusion among the poor measures whether schemes such as Jan Dhan translate into real access.

series.note: Poorest 40% with an Account: India's annual series, 2011 to 2024; the latest value is 86.32%. Source: World Bank API FX.OWN.TOTL.40.ZS (World Bank Global Findex / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Adult Account Ownership: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of adults with a financial account. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Compare India's catch-up with peers that started from similar levels.

Why it matters — Account ownership is the first step to digital payments, savings and credit.

series.note: Adult Account Ownership: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API FX.OWN.TOTL.ZS (World Bank Global Findex / IMF); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Stock Market Capitalisation
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Market value of all listed domestic companies as a share of GDP. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 266.92% of GDP in 2025. Higher shows a deeper equity market relative to the economy.

Why it matters — Market depth indicates how easily firms can raise equity.

series.note: Stock Market Capitalisation: India's annual series, 2000 to 2025; the latest value is 266.92% of GDP. Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Stock Market Capitalisation: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Market value of all listed domestic companies as a share of GDP. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Higher shows a deeper equity market relative to the economy.

Why it matters — Market depth indicates how easily firms can raise equity.

series.note: Stock Market Capitalisation: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Stock Market Capitalisation: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Market value of all listed domestic companies as a share of GDP. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 2 of 11 (1 = highest value). Higher shows a deeper equity market relative to the economy.

Why it matters — Market depth indicates how easily firms can raise equity.

series.note: Stock Market Capitalisation, 2025: India ranks 2 of 11 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.LCAP.GD.ZS (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Stocks Traded
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total value of shares traded in a year relative to GDP. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 72.66% of GDP in 2025. Higher means a more actively traded, liquid market.

Why it matters — Liquidity lowers the cost of capital and attracts investors.

series.note: Stocks Traded: India's annual series, 2000 to 2025; the latest value is 72.66% of GDP. Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.TRAD.GD.ZS (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Stocks Traded: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 4 of 11 (1 = highest value). Higher means a more actively traded, liquid market.

Why it matters — Liquidity lowers the cost of capital and attracts investors.

series.note: Stocks Traded, 2025: India ranks 4 of 11 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.TRAD.GD.ZS (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Listed Domestic Companies
indicators.subtitle: India, 1983-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Number of domestic companies listed on the country's exchanges. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 8,510 companies in 2025. A larger bar or slice means a wider choice of listed businesses.

Why it matters — Listing count reflects how broad the corporate base is that can access public equity.

series.note: Listed Domestic Companies: India's annual series, 1983 to 2025; the latest value is 8,510 companies. Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.LDOM.NO (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 2 of 11 (1 = highest value). A larger bar or slice means a wider choice of listed businesses.

Why it matters — Listing count reflects how broad the corporate base is that can access public equity.

indicators.title: S&P Global Equity Index Change
indicators.subtitle: India, 1996-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual percentage change in the S&P Global equity index for each country. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 0.11% in 2025. Bars above zero are rising years; large drops mark market crashes.

Why it matters — Equity returns drive household wealth and the attractiveness of retail investing.

series.note: S&P Global Equity Index Change: India's annual series, 1996 to 2025; the latest value is 0.11%. Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.INDX.ZG (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

Why it matters — Equity returns drive household wealth and the attractiveness of retail investing.

series.note: S&P Global Equity Index Change: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API CM.MKT.INDX.ZG (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Portfolio Equity Net Inflows
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Net foreign purchases of equity securities, in US dollars. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at -18.54 USD bn in 2025. Spikes are foreign buying sprees; negative values are net outflows.

Why it matters — Portfolio flows are volatile and move the rupee and stock prices.

series.note: Portfolio Equity Net Inflows: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is -18.54 USD bn. Source: World Bank API BX.PEF.TOTL.CD.WD (World Bank Financial Development / IMF BoP); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: NITI Fiscal Health Index: composite score by state (FY2023)
indicators.subtitle: Composite FHI score for 18 major states, higher is healthier
indicators.details:
What it shows — NITI Aayog's composite score of state fiscal health for FY2023, built from five sub-indices on expenditure quality, revenue mobilisation, fiscal prudence, debt and debt sustainability.

How to read it — Odisha tops the index at 67.8; Punjab is lowest at 10.7. Scores compare states with each other rather than against a fixed norm.

Why it matters — States account for about two-thirds of general government spending, so their balance sheets shape the national fiscal outlook.

datasets.label: NITI Fiscal Health Index: composite score by state (FY2023)

series.note: Fiscal Health Index 2025, Annual Report for the Financial Year 2023 (NITI Aayog, January 2025). Himalayan and North-Eastern states are not covered. Composite of quality of expenditure, revenue mobilisation, fiscal prudence, debt index and debt sustainability.

indicators.title: Basic Drinking Water: Urban vs Rural India
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of urban and rural populations using at least a basic drinking-water service.

How to read it — The distance between the lines is the rural deficit; converging lines mean the gap is closing.

Why it matters — Rural water access is central to the health gains targeted by regional programmes.

series.note: Basic Drinking Water: Urban vs Rural India, 2000 to 2024. Source: World Bank API SH.H2O.BASW.UR.ZS, SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS (WHO / UNICEF JMP / World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Basic Sanitation: Urban vs Rural India
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of urban and rural people using at least basic sanitation facilities.

How to read it — A steeper rural line means faster catch-up after the Swachh Bharat push.

Why it matters — Sanitation gaps drive diarrhoeal disease and child stunting in rural regions.

series.note: Basic Sanitation: Urban vs Rural India, 2000 to 2024. Source: World Bank API SH.STA.BASS.UR.ZS, SH.STA.BASS.RU.ZS (WHO / UNICEF JMP / World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Electricity Access: Urban vs Rural India
indicators.subtitle: India, 1993-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of urban and rural populations with access to electricity.

How to read it — Both lines near 100% mean the divide has effectively closed.

Why it matters — Electrification is the precondition for rural clinics, schools and enterprises.

series.note: Electricity Access: Urban vs Rural India, 1993 to 2024. Source: World Bank API EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS, EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS (WHO / UNICEF JMP / World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Open Defecation: Urban vs Rural India
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of urban and rural people practising open defecation.

How to read it — Falling lines are progress; the rural line starts much higher.

Why it matters — Open defecation is a direct driver of infection and malnutrition.

series.note: Open Defecation: Urban vs Rural India, 2000 to 2024. Source: World Bank API SH.STA.ODFC.UR.ZS, SH.STA.ODFC.RU.ZS (WHO / UNICEF JMP / World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Population: Urban vs Rural India
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Absolute urban and rural population living in India.

How to read it — Where the lines cross shows when urban numbers overtake rural ones; rural numbers are flattening.

Why it matters — The balance of urban and rural people drives service demand across states.

series.note: Population: Urban vs Rural India, 1980 to 2025. Source: World Bank API SP.URB.TOTL, SP.RUR.TOTL (WHO / UNICEF JMP / World Bank); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Urban-Rural Gap in Basic Water Access: Peer Ranking (2024)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Urban minus rural share of people with basic drinking water, in percentage points. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2024; India ranks 7 of 14 (1 = highest value). Bigger bars are bigger rural disadvantages; near zero means equal access.

Why it matters — The gap pinpoints where rural investment is still lagging.

datasets.label: Urban-Rural Gap in Basic Water Access: Peer Ranking (2024)

series.note: Urban-Rural Gap in Basic Water Access, 2024: India ranks 7 of 14 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API SH.H2O.BASW.UR.ZS, SH.H2O.BASW.RU.ZS (WHO / UNICEF JMP / World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Urban-Rural Gap in Basic Sanitation: Peer Ranking (2024)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Urban minus rural share of people with basic sanitation, in percentage points. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2024; India ranks 4 of 14 (1 = highest value). Larger positive bars show rural populations being left behind.

Why it matters — Closing this gap is a prerequisite for equal health outcomes across regions.

datasets.label: Urban-Rural Gap in Basic Sanitation: Peer Ranking (2024)

series.note: Urban-Rural Gap in Basic Sanitation, 2024: India ranks 4 of 14 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API SH.STA.BASS.UR.ZS, SH.STA.BASS.RU.ZS (WHO / UNICEF JMP / World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of the urban population living in the country's largest city. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 6.64% of urban population in 2025. Low values mean urban growth is spread over many cities rather than concentrated.

Why it matters — Dispersed urbanisation reduces pressure on a single megacity.

series.note: Population in Largest City: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 6.64% of urban population. Source: World Bank API EN.URB.LCTY.UR.ZS (UN World Urbanization Prospects via World Bank); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: IIP growth
indicators.subtitle: Industrial production
indicators.details:
Industrial production measures activity across mining, manufacturing, and electricity. It is a useful complement to GDP because it responds more directly to changes in factory output and infrastructure-linked production.

The monthly General IIP index is collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.2; MOSPI remains the authoritative Indian source.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: WPI inflation
indicators.subtitle: Wholesale price inflation
indicators.details:
Wholesale price inflation tracks price movement at the producer and bulk-trade level. It can reveal input-cost pressure before those changes fully appear in consumer prices.

WPI is not included in the Economic Survey monthly HFI tables used by this pipeline. The Office of the Economic Adviser remains the official source, but its public portal does not currently expose a stable automated export for this dashboard.

indicators.title: Power consumption
indicators.subtitle: Electricity demand
indicators.details:
Power consumption is a high-frequency activity signal that reflects demand from households, services, and industry. It can move with weather, economic activity, and electrification.

The monthly series is collated from Economic Survey Statistical Appendix table 9.1. It measures electricity use, not generation capacity or reliability.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: E-way bills
indicators.subtitle: Goods movement compliance volume
indicators.details:
E-way bills track electronically documented movement of goods. They provide a useful logistics and formal-commerce signal that complements GST collections.

The series is a transaction volume, not a rupee value or direct GDP estimate. It is collated from Economic Survey table 9.1.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Rail freight traffic
indicators.subtitle: Domestic rail freight
indicators.details:
Rail freight traffic reflects movement of bulk commodities and industrial inputs through the rail network. It provides a physical-economy signal alongside digital and tax indicators.

The series is reported in thousand tonnes and comes from Economic Survey table 9.1.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: Port cargo traffic
indicators.subtitle: Cargo handled at ports
indicators.details:
Port cargo traffic captures goods handled through India's ports and gives context for external trade and domestic supply chains.

It is a volume measure and should be read with merchandise exports, imports, and trade share rather than used as a price indicator.

series.source: Economic Survey Statistical Appendix tables 9.1-9.4 across 2022-23 to latest edition

indicators.title: India: Sector Composition of Value Added (2025)
indicators.subtitle: India, shares of total, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — India's value added split across agriculture, industry (including construction and mining) and services.

How to read it — Larger slices dominate output; services typically lead as an economy matures. In 2025, Services is the largest slice at 54.4%.

Why it matters — The split shows how far India's structural transformation has progressed.

series.note: India: Sector Composition of Value Added, 2025: Services is the largest slice at 54.4%. Source: World Bank API NV.AGR.TOTL.CD, NV.IND.TOTL.CD, NV.SRV.TOTL.CD (World Bank national accounts / ILO); latest year with data: 2025.
series.source: World Bank API NV.AGR.TOTL.CD, NV.IND.TOTL.CD, NV.SRV.TOTL.CD

indicators.title: GDP per Person Employed
indicators.subtitle: India, 1991-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Output per worker in constant 2021 PPP dollars, a standard measure of labour productivity. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 24,842.11 PPP $ per worker in 2025. A rising line means each worker produces more; the gap to peers shows the productivity deficit.

Why it matters — Productivity growth is the only sustainable route to higher wages.

indicators.title: Energy Intensity of GDP
indicators.subtitle: India, 1990-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Energy use per 1,000 dollars of GDP at PPP, a measure of how efficiently an economy uses energy. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 82.47 kg oil eq per $1,000 in 2024. A falling line means India squeezes more output from each unit of energy.

Why it matters — Lower energy intensity reduces import bills and emissions for every rupee of growth.

series.note: Energy Intensity of GDP: India's annual series, 1990 to 2024; the latest value is 82.47 kg oil eq per $1,000. Source: World Bank API EG.USE.COMM.GD.PP.KD (IEA / World Bank energy statistics); latest year with data: 2024.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. A falling line means India squeezes more output from each unit of energy.

Why it matters — Lower energy intensity reduces import bills and emissions for every rupee of growth.

series.note: Energy Intensity of GDP: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API EG.USE.COMM.GD.PP.KD (IEA / World Bank energy statistics); latest year with data: 2024.

series.note: Mean of the reported annual values inside each decade, using decades with at least two observations. Source indicator(s): BX.GSR.CCIS.CD.

indicators.title: ICT Share of Service Exports: India Trend
indicators.subtitle: ICT services as a share of total service exports.
indicators.details:
What it shows — ICT services as a share of total service exports.

How to read it — The line plots India's own history from 2000 to 2025; the last point is 48.60% svc exports.

Why it matters — A high share shows how strongly India's services trade depends on software and IT outsourcing.

datasets.label: ICT Share of Service Exports: India Trend

series.note: India's annual series from 2000 to 2025; years without a reported value are omitted. Source indicator(s): BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS.

indicators.title: ICT Share of Service Exports: India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: ICT Share of Service Exports for India and six major comparison economies
indicators.details:
What it shows — ICT services as a share of total service exports, compared across India and six large economies.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the higher the line, the stronger that country's position.

Why it matters — A high share shows how strongly India's services trade depends on software and IT outsourcing.

series.note: India (orange) against China, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Germany and Brazil. Plotted in each country's own units. Source indicator(s): BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS.

indicators.title: ICT Share of Service Exports: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: ICT Share of Service Exports, India against 14 peer economies
indicators.details:
What it shows — ICT services as a share of total service exports.

How to read it — Bars are sorted from highest to lowest; India ranks 2 of 14 at 48.60% svc exports.

Why it matters — A high share shows how strongly India's services trade depends on software and IT outsourcing.

datasets.label: ICT Share of Service Exports: Peer Ranking (2025)

series.note: Latest value per country within three years of India's 2025 observation (WB data). India ranks 2 of 14 in this peer group. Source indicator(s): BX.GSR.CCIS.ZS.

indicators.title: Mobile connectivity in LWE-affected villages
indicators.subtitle: Villages with mobile coverage out of villages in LWE areas
indicators.details:
What it shows — How many villages in LWE-affected areas have mobile coverage.

How to read it — About 96 percent of villages are covered.

Why it matters — Mobile coverage supports tip-offs, welfare delivery and digital payments.

series.note: PIB backgrounder "Naxal-Free India: Integrated Strategies Defeated Left-Wing Extremism" (Ministry of Home Affairs, 1 August 2026): 44,728 of 46,592 villages covered (96 percent).

indicators.title: Route Length Since Independence
indicators.subtitle: Route kilometres of Indian Railways
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total route kilometres across all gauges, 1950-51 to 2023-24.

How to read it — The network grew by about 15,600 km over 73 years and stood at 69,181 km on 31 March 2024.

Why it matters — Route length is the physical reach of the railway.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', route kilometres since 1950-51; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Route vs Track Kilometres
indicators.subtitle: Doubling and multi-tracking since 1950-51
indicators.details:
What it shows — Route, running-track and total-track kilometres.

How to read it — Running track grew about 85% since 1950-51 against 29% for route length, which points to doubling and extra lines on existing corridors.

Why it matters — Track length divided by route length shows how much of the network has more than one line.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', route, running track and total track kilometres; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Cumulative Electrified Route
indicators.subtitle: Electrified route kilometres, 1951 to 2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cumulative electrified route kilometres in each year shown.

How to read it — Electrification more than tripled after 2011; a record 4,644 km was electrified in 2023-24, taking the total to 62,253 km, about 90% of the broad-gauge network.

Why it matters — The Mission 100% Electrification policy aims to cut diesel imports and running costs.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'Electrification', cumulative electrified route kilometres; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 74-78.

indicators.title: Route Length by Gauge (2023-24)
indicators.subtitle: Broad, metre and narrow gauge route kilometres
indicators.details:
What it shows — Route kilometres by track gauge on 31 March 2024.

How to read it — Broad gauge is 96.59% of the route and carried 100% of freight output and 99.96% of passenger-km.

Why it matters — A single dominant gauge lets trains run end to end across the country.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', route length by gauge on 31 March 2024; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Route Kilometres by Zonal Railway (2023-24)
indicators.subtitle: Route length of the 16 zones plus Kolkata Metro
indicators.details:
What it shows — Route kilometres under each of the 16 zonal railways and Metro Railway Kolkata.

How to read it — Northern Railway (7,406 km), South Central (6,610) and Western (6,284) run the longest networks.

Why it matters — Zones are the operating units of Indian Railways.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', route kilometres by zonal railway, 2023-24; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Route Kilometres by State (2023-24)
indicators.subtitle: Railway route length in each state and union territory
indicators.details:
What it shows — Route kilometres within each state or union territory at the end of 2023-24.

How to read it — Uttar Pradesh (8,823 km), Rajasthan (6,135) and Maharashtra (5,930) have the longest networks; Mizoram has 1 km.

Why it matters — State-wise length shows where rail access is deepest.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', state-wise route kilometres, 2023-24. States and territories not listed have no railway line; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Running Track per 100 Route-Km
indicators.subtitle: Running-track length relative to route length
indicators.details:
What it shows — Running-track kilometres for every 100 route-kilometres, calculated from the Year Book series.

How to read it — The ratio was 158.64 in 2023-24, versus 110.67 in 1950-51.

Why it matters — It indicates how much additional track exists beyond a single route line.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', route and running track kilometres; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Route-Km Added Between Benchmarks
indicators.subtitle: Change in route length since the prior listed year
indicators.details:
What it shows — Difference between each adjacent published route-kilometre benchmark.

How to read it — The listed route length increased by 15,585 km from 1950-51 to 2023-24; the last interval added 597 km.

Why it matters — The differences show when network expansion accelerated or slowed.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', route kilometres by benchmark year; each bar is the change from the preceding listed benchmark; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Route Length Index
indicators.subtitle: Route kilometres indexed to 1950-51
indicators.details:
What it shows — Route kilometres as an index, with 1950-51 set to 100.

How to read it — The index reached 129.1 in 2023-24.

Why it matters — An index makes long-run growth easier to compare.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'The Network', route kilometres since 1950-51; index calculated from the published values; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62.

indicators.title: Electrified Route Share
indicators.subtitle: Electrified kilometres as a share of route kilometres
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cumulative electrified route kilometres divided by total route kilometres.

How to read it — The ratio was 89.99% in the 2023-24 benchmark.

Why it matters — It tracks the reach of electrification across the network.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): 'Electrification' cumulative electrified route and 'The Network' route kilometres; share calculated for matching benchmark years; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 60-62 and 74-78.

indicators.title: Passengers Originating
indicators.subtitle: Annual passenger journeys on Indian Railways
indicators.details:
What it shows — Passenger journeys that began on Indian Railways, in millions.

How to read it — Journeys fell to 1,250 million in 2020-21 (COVID-19) and recovered to 6,905 million in 2023-24, still below the 7,651 million of 2010-11.

Why it matters — It is the headline demand measure for Indian Railways.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table I (passengers originating, suburban plus non-suburban); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Suburban vs Non-Suburban Journeys
indicators.subtitle: Passengers originating by service type
indicators.details:
What it shows — Suburban (city commuter) and non-suburban (long-distance) passenger journeys.

How to read it — Suburban journeys were 3,981 million in 2023-24, 58% of the total.

Why it matters — Commuter and long-distance services need different capacity.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table I, suburban versus non-suburban journeys; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Passenger Kilometres
indicators.subtitle: Total distance travelled by rail passengers
indicators.details:
What it shows — Passenger-kilometres: each passenger multiplied by the distance travelled.

How to read it — Output reached 1,064,700 million passenger-km in 2023-24, about 16 times the 1950-51 level and above 2010-11.

Why it matters — Passenger-km measures output; counting journeys alone ignores how far people travel.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table II (passenger kilometres); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Average Passenger Journey Length
indicators.subtitle: Average lead per passenger
indicators.details:
What it shows — Average distance of a passenger journey, in kilometres.

How to read it — It rose from 51.8 km in 1950-51 to 154.2 km in 2023-24, with a peak of 184.8 km in 2020-21.

Why it matters — A longer lead means a bigger share of travel is intercity rather than suburban.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table III (average lead of all passengers); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Passenger Journeys by Service (2023-24)
indicators.subtitle: Split of 6,905 million journeys
indicators.details:
What it shows — How 2023-24 passenger journeys split across suburban and non-suburban classes.

How to read it — Suburban is 57.7% of journeys, second-class mail/express 27.1%, second-class ordinary 10.6% and upper class 4.6%.

Why it matters — Most journeys are suburban or second class.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table I, 2023-24 journeys by service and class; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Trains Run Daily
indicators.subtitle: Passenger and goods trains on an average day
indicators.details:
What it shows — Average number of passenger and goods trains run each day.

How to read it — Passenger trains per day grew 5.2% and goods trains 12.9% between 2022-23 and 2023-24.

Why it matters — Train counts show how intensively the track is used.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, Train Utilisation; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

indicators.title: Suburban Share of Journeys
indicators.subtitle: Suburban journeys as a share of all passenger journeys
indicators.details:
What it shows — Suburban passenger journeys divided by total passenger journeys for each year.

How to read it — Suburban journeys were 57.65% of the 2023-24 total.

Why it matters — The share distinguishes commuter traffic from long-distance demand.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table I, suburban journeys divided by total journeys; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Non-Suburban Share of Journeys
indicators.subtitle: Non-suburban journeys as a share of all passenger journeys
indicators.details:
What it shows — Non-suburban passenger journeys divided by total passenger journeys for each year.

How to read it — Non-suburban journeys were 42.35% of the 2023-24 total.

Why it matters — This share tracks the long-distance portion of passenger traffic.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table I, non-suburban journeys divided by total journeys; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Calculated Average Passenger Journey
indicators.subtitle: Passenger-km divided by passenger journeys
indicators.details:
What it shows — Average journey length calculated from passenger-kilometres and journeys originating.

How to read it — The ratio was 154.19 km per journey in 2023-24; it is calculated independently of the reported average lead.

Why it matters — It cross-checks the relationship between passenger volume and distance travelled.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Tables I and II; passenger-km divided by passengers originating; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Passenger-Km Index
indicators.subtitle: Passenger-kilometres indexed to 1950-51
indicators.details:
What it shows — Passenger-kilometres as an index with 1950-51 set to 100.

How to read it — The index reached 1600.6 in 2023-24.

Why it matters — The index shows long-run growth in passenger transport work.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Passenger Business, Table II; passenger-kilometres indexed to 1950-51; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 22-37.

indicators.title: Freight Originating
indicators.subtitle: Revenue-earning tonnes loaded by Indian Railways
indicators.details:
What it shows — Revenue-earning freight originating on Indian Railways, in million tonnes.

How to read it — From 73 million tonnes in 1950-51 to 1,588 million tonnes in 2023-24, about 21.7 times higher.

Why it matters — Rail carries the bulk commodities (coal, ore, cement, foodgrains) that supply industry.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I (revenue-earning freight, tonnes originating, excluding Konkan Railway); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Freight Output (Net Tonne-Km)
indicators.subtitle: Tonnes moved multiplied by distance
indicators.details:
What it shows — Net tonne-kilometres: freight tonnage multiplied by distance moved.

How to read it — Output reached 973,968 million NTKM in 2023-24, about 26 times 1950-51.

Why it matters — NTKM measures transport work; tonnes alone ignore haul length.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I (net tonne kilometres); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Average Freight Haul
indicators.subtitle: Average lead of a tonne of freight
indicators.details:
What it shows — Average distance a tonne of freight is carried.

How to read it — Average haul peaked at 754 km in 1980-81 and was 613 km in 2023-24.

Why it matters — Haul length affects wagon use and freight earnings per tonne.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I (average lead of freight); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Freight by Commodity (2023-24)
indicators.subtitle: Share of 1,588 million tonnes loaded
indicators.details:
What it shows — Revenue-earning freight by commodity group in 2023-24.

How to read it — Coal is 49.55% of loading (thermal power houses alone 38.19%), then iron ore 11.39%, cement 9.62% and containers 5.34%.

Why it matters — Rail freight depends heavily on bulk coal.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, commodity-wise loading 2023-24; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Commodity Loading: 2022-23 vs 2023-24
indicators.subtitle: Tonnes loaded by commodity group
indicators.details:
What it shows — Tonnes carried for each commodity group in the last two years.

How to read it — Coal added 59.6 million tonnes and iron ore 20.8 million; foodgrains fell by 19.5 million.

Why it matters — Year-on-year changes show which commodities drove growth.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, commodity-wise loading 2022-23 vs 2023-24; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Freight Loading to 2024-25
indicators.subtitle: Originating loading, latest Ministry figures
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total originating freight loading, from Ministry of Railways statements.

How to read it — Loading reached 1,617.38 million tonnes in 2024-25; the Ministry says this makes Indian Railways the second-largest freight carrier in the world.

Why it matters — It extends the series past the Year Book's 2023-24 end year.

series.note: Ministry of Railways via PIB: originating freight loading was 1,233 MT in 2020-21 (Lok Sabha reply, PIB release 2201815), 1,590.68 MT in 2023-24 and 1,617.38 MT in 2024-25, up 1.68% (PIB release 2117417, 1 April 2025, opening freight-loading paragraph). These cover all originating loading, so they differ slightly from the Year Book's revenue-earning series.

indicators.title: Commodity Shares of Loading
indicators.subtitle: Commodity tonnes as a share of 2023-24 revenue-earning loading
indicators.details:
What it shows — Each commodity group's reported loading divided by total revenue-earning tonnes originating.

How to read it — Coal accounted for 49.55% of 2023-24 revenue-earning loading.

Why it matters — The shares show the commodity concentration of rail freight.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation commodity table, 2023-24 loading as a share of the 1,588.06 million tonnes reported in Table I; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Commodity Loading Growth
indicators.subtitle: Percent change in tonnes loaded by commodity
indicators.details:
What it shows — Year-on-year percentage change in commodity loading between 2022-23 and 2023-24.

How to read it — Coal loading rose 8.20%; foodgrains changed by -27.47%.

Why it matters — Growth by commodity identifies which goods gained or lost loading.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation commodity-wise loading table, 2022-23 to 2023-24; percentage changes calculated from table values; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Calculated Average Freight Haul
indicators.subtitle: Net tonne-km divided by originating tonnes
indicators.details:
What it shows — Average freight haul calculated by dividing net tonne-kilometres by tonnes originating.

How to read it — The calculated average haul was 613.31 km in 2023-24.

Why it matters — The quotient ties freight volume to the distance moved.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I; net tonne-kilometres divided by revenue-earning tonnes; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Freight Loading Change Between Benchmarks
indicators.subtitle: Change in originating tonnes since the prior listed year
indicators.details:
What it shows — Difference in revenue-earning tonnes originating between adjacent listed benchmark years.

How to read it — Loading increased by 78.96 million tonnes between 2022-23 and 2023-24.

Why it matters — The changes reveal the varying scale of long-run growth.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Freight Operation, Table I; change between adjacent listed originating-tonnage benchmarks; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 38-45.

indicators.title: Locomotives by Traction (2023-24)
indicators.subtitle: 15,110 locomotives by type
indicators.details:
What it shows — Locomotive fleet by traction type on 31 March 2024.

How to read it — Electric locomotives are 70.7% of the fleet; 38 steam locomotives remain.

Why it matters — Fleet mix follows the electrification of the route.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, locomotives on 31 March 2024; Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

indicators.title: Locomotive Fleet: 2022-23 vs 2023-24
indicators.subtitle: Locomotives by traction type
indicators.details:
What it shows — Number of electric, diesel and steam locomotives in the last two years.

How to read it — Electric locomotives grew by 1,110 while diesel fell by 333.

Why it matters — Shows the shift from diesel to electric traction year by year.

series.note: Ministry of Railways, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24 (Directorate of Statistics & Economics, Railway Board): Other Important Statistics, number of locomotives (2022-23 revised); Year Book 2023-24, pp. 4-6.

indicators.title: Coach Fleet: 2022-23 vs 2023-24
indicators.subtitle: Passenger and other coaching vehicles
indicators.details:
