indicators.title: Merchandise Exports
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Value of goods exported, in current US dollars. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 445.28 USD bn in 2025. Higher bars show larger goods-trading nations; India's slice shows its share of the group's exports.

Why it matters — Goods exports reflect industrial competitiveness and supply-chain integration.

series.note: Merchandise Exports: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is 445.28 USD bn. Source: World Bank API TX.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Merchandise Exports: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Value of goods exported, in current US dollars. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 7 of 15 (1 = highest value). Higher bars show larger goods-trading nations; India's slice shows its share of the group's exports.

Why it matters — Goods exports reflect industrial competitiveness and supply-chain integration.

series.note: Merchandise Exports, 2025: India ranks 7 of 15 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API TX.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Merchandise Exports: Share Among Peers (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Each country's share of the 15-country total
indicators.details:
What it shows — Value of goods exported, in current US dollars. Slices show each country's share of the sampled countries' total.

How to read it — Slices are shares of the group total in 2025; India holds 3.9% and ranks 7 of 15. A bigger slice means a larger absolute amount, not a better outcome.

Why it matters — Goods exports reflect industrial competitiveness and supply-chain integration.

series.note: Merchandise Exports, 2025: India holds 3.9% of the group total and ranks 7 of 15. Source: World Bank API TX.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Merchandise Trade Balance
indicators.subtitle: India, 1980-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Merchandise exports minus merchandise imports, in US dollars. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at -308.2 USD bn in 2025. Negative values are trade deficits; positive are surpluses.

Why it matters — India's chronic goods deficit shapes the current account and the rupee.

series.note: Merchandise Trade Balance: India's annual series, 1980 to 2025; the latest value is -308.2 USD bn. Source: World Bank API TX.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT, TM.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Merchandise Trade Balance: Peer Ranking (2025)
indicators.subtitle: Countries ranked highest to lowest, 2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Merchandise exports minus merchandise imports, in US dollars. Fifteen countries are ranked on the latest year with broad coverage.

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2025; India ranks 13 of 15 (1 = highest value). Negative values are trade deficits; positive are surpluses.

Why it matters — India's chronic goods deficit shapes the current account and the rupee.

series.note: Merchandise Trade Balance, 2025: India ranks 13 of 15 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API TX.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT, TM.VAL.MRCH.CD.WT (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.title: Export Volume Index (2015 = 100)
indicators.subtitle: India, 2005-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Quantity of goods exported, stripped of price effects, with 2015 set to 100. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 138.1 index in 2024. A steeper rise means the physical volume of exports is growing faster.

Why it matters — Volume shows real export capacity independent of commodity-price swings.

series.note: Export Volume Index (2015 = 100): India's annual series, 2005 to 2024; the latest value is 138.1 index. Source: World Bank API TX.QTY.MRCH.XD.WD (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Export Volume Index (2015 = 100): India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Quantity of goods exported, stripped of price effects, with 2015 set to 100. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. A steeper rise means the physical volume of exports is growing faster.

Why it matters — Volume shows real export capacity independent of commodity-price swings.

series.note: Export Volume Index (2015 = 100): India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API TX.QTY.MRCH.XD.WD (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Net Barter Terms of Trade (2015 = 100)
indicators.subtitle: India, 2005-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Export prices relative to import prices; higher means each unit of exports buys more imports. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 91.3 index in 2024. A falling line means imports are getting dearer relative to exports.

Why it matters — Terms of trade drive real income gains and losses from trade.

series.note: Net Barter Terms of Trade (2015 = 100): India's annual series, 2005 to 2024; the latest value is 91.3 index. Source: World Bank API TT.PRI.MRCH.XD.WD (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Net Barter Terms of Trade (2015 = 100): India vs Peers
indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours
indicators.details:
What it shows — Export prices relative to import prices; higher means each unit of exports buys more imports. This chart overlays India with 6 comparison countries.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. A falling line means imports are getting dearer relative to exports.

Why it matters — Terms of trade drive real income gains and losses from trade.

series.note: Net Barter Terms of Trade (2015 = 100): India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API TT.PRI.MRCH.XD.WD (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: Applied Tariff Rate

Why it matters — Tariff levels shape the cost of inputs and India's access to global value chains.

series.note: Applied Tariff Rate: India's annual series, 1990 to 2022; the latest value is 4.59%. Source: World Bank API TM.TAX.MRCH.WM.AR.ZS (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2022.

indicators.details:

How to read it — Bars run from highest to lowest in 2022; India ranks 6 of 13 (1 = highest value). Lower values mean freer trade; bars show how protected each economy is.

Why it matters — Tariff levels shape the cost of inputs and India's access to global value chains.

series.note: Applied Tariff Rate, 2022: India ranks 6 of 13 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API TM.TAX.MRCH.WM.AR.ZS (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2022.

indicators.title: Logistics Performance Index
indicators.subtitle: India, 2007-2022
indicators.details:
What it shows — World Bank survey score (1 to 5) covering customs, infrastructure, shipments, tracking and timeliness. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 3.4 score in 2022. A higher score means smoother and cheaper movement of goods.

Why it matters — Logistics efficiency is a major hidden cost in Indian manufacturing.

series.note: Logistics Performance Index: India's annual series, 2007 to 2022; the latest value is 3.4 score. Source: World Bank API LP.LPI.OVRL.XQ (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2022.

indicators.title: Logistics Performance Index: Peer Ranking (2022)

Why it matters — Logistics efficiency is a major hidden cost in Indian manufacturing.

series.note: Logistics Performance Index, 2022: India ranks 8 of 13 (1 = highest value). Source: World Bank API LP.LPI.OVRL.XQ (World Bank / WTO / UNCTAD trade statistics); latest year with data: 2022.

indicators.title: National Highway Network
indicators.subtitle: National Highway network length
indicators.details:
What it shows — Length of India's National Highway network at the stated dates.

How to read it — The reported network expanded by about 60% from 2014 to 2024.

Why it matters — National Highways form the long-distance road backbone for freight.

series.note: MoRTH Year End Review 2024 (PIB): National Highway network length was 91,287 km in 2014 and 146,195 km in 2024.

indicators.title: Four-Lane-and-Above National Highways
indicators.subtitle: NH length with four or more lanes
indicators.details:
What it shows — Length of National Highways with four or more lanes.

How to read it — The reported extent increased from 18,387 km in 2014 to 46,179 km by November 2023.

Why it matters — More divided-lane highway capacity can improve freight movement and reduce bottlenecks.

series.note: MoRTH Year End Review 2023 (PIB): length of National Highways with four or more lanes.

indicators.title: Bharatmala Phase I Progress
indicators.subtitle: Awarded versus constructed project length
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cumulative lengths of Bharatmala Phase I projects awarded and constructed.

How to read it — 26,425 km had been awarded and 19,826 km constructed by 28 February 2025.

Why it matters — The gap distinguishes tendered projects from completed road capacity.

series.note: MoRTH parliamentary reply / PIB, 13 March 2025: Bharatmala Phase I project lengths awarded and constructed as at 28 February 2025.

indicators.title: High-Speed Greenfield Corridors
indicators.subtitle: Awarded versus constructed length
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cumulative awarded and constructed lengths of high-speed greenfield corridors.

How to read it — Of 6,669 km awarded, 4,610 km was completed by 28 February 2025.

Why it matters — Shows progress on high-capacity road links between economic centres.

series.note: MoRTH PIB release, 13 March 2025: high-speed greenfield corridor length awarded and completed as at 28 February 2025.

indicators.title: FASTag Share of Toll Payments
indicators.subtitle: NHAI toll transactions, FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of NHAI toll payments collected through FASTag; remainder is calculated.

How to read it — FASTag accounted for 98.5%; other methods make up the derived 1.5% remainder.

Why it matters — Electronic collection measures payment digitisation, not freight tonnage.

series.note: NHAI Annual Report 2023-24: 98.5% of toll payments were collected through FASTag. Other-payment share is the arithmetic complement, not a separately reported statistic.

indicators.title: FASTag Collections
indicators.subtitle: FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — Approximate toll collection through FASTag during FY 2023-24.

How to read it — NHAI reports around Rs 55,000 crore collected through FASTag.

Why it matters — User-fee collection for highway tolls, not road-freight operator turnover.

series.note: NHAI Annual Report 2023-24, Electronic Toll Collection: FASTag collection was around Rs 55,000 crore in FY 2023-24 (IHMCL source).

indicators.title: NHAI Awards and Construction
indicators.subtitle: National Highway length in FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — National Highway lengths awarded and constructed by NHAI during FY 2023-24.

How to read it — NHAI constructed 6,644 km, its highest annual construction achievement reported in the annual report.

Why it matters — Annual delivery indicates the pace of road capacity being added.

series.note: NHAI Annual Report 2023-24: NHAI awarded 3,339 km and constructed 6,644 km of National Highways during FY 2023-24.

indicators.title: National Highway Network Growth Index
indicators.details:
What it shows — Rounded NH network length index derived from MoRTH's reported 60% growth.

How to read it — The 2023 index is 160 when 2014 is 100; it is derived, not an observed km series.

Why it matters — An index communicates proportional expansion without treating rounded endpoints as exact growth.

series.note: MoRTH Year End Review 2023 reports NH length rose 60% from 91,287 km in 2014 to 146,145 km in 2023; displayed index expresses its rounded growth as 160.

indicators.title: Rail Freight Loading
indicators.subtitle: Revenue-earning tonnes originating
indicators.details:
What it shows — Revenue-earning freight originating on Indian Railways, in million tonnes.

How to read it — Loading reached 1,588.06 million tonnes in 2023-24; this is the Year Book revenue-earning series, not all-originating loading.

Why it matters — Repeats railway output in the cross-mode dashboard without altering the rail group's chart.

series.note: Railway Board, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24, Freight Operation Table I: revenue-earning freight tonnes originating (excluding Konkan Railway).

indicators.title: Rail Freight Transport Work
indicators.subtitle: Net tonne-kilometres
indicators.details:
What it shows — Net tonne-kilometres: tonnes multiplied by distance carried.

How to read it — Indian Railways recorded 973,968 million net tonne-km in 2023-24.

Why it matters — Tonne-km includes freight volume and haul distance, unlike tonnes alone.

series.note: Railway Board, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24, Freight Operation Table I (net tonne-kilometres).

indicators.title: Rail Freight by Commodity
indicators.subtitle: 2023-24 originating loading
indicators.details:
What it shows — Revenue-earning rail freight tonnes by commodity group in 2023-24.

How to read it — Coal loading was 786.84 million tonnes, 49.55% of the 1,588.06 million tonne total.

Why it matters — The commodity mix shows dependence on bulk and industrial goods.

series.note: Railway Board, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24, Freight Operation: commodity-wise revenue-earning loading in 2023-24.

indicators.title: Rail Loading by Commodity: Year-on-Year
indicators.subtitle: Commodity-wise revenue-earning loading
indicators.details:
What it shows — Freight loading by commodity group in FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24.

How to read it — Coal rose from 727.24 to 786.84 million tonnes; foodgrains fell from 70.92 to 51.44 million tonnes.

Why it matters — A same-commodity comparison helps identify sources of freight growth.

series.note: Railway Board, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24, Freight Operation: commodity-wise revenue-earning tonnes originating, 2022-23 and 2023-24.

indicators.title: Rail Freight Average Lead
indicators.subtitle: Average distance per tonne
indicators.details:
What it shows — Average distance carried for each tonne of railway freight.

How to read it — Average freight lead was 613 km in 2023-24.

Why it matters — Average lead puts freight tonnes in the context of distance moved.

series.note: Railway Board, Indian Railways Year Book 2023-24, Freight Operation Table I: average lead of freight.

indicators.title: Dedicated Freight Corridor Progress
indicators.subtitle: EDFC and WDFC route kilometres
indicators.details:
What it shows — Operational route kilometres compared with combined EDFC and WDFC length.

How to read it — 2,741 of 2,843 route-km (96.4%) was operational in March 2025.

Why it matters — Dedicated corridors add freight capacity separate from much of the passenger network.

series.note: Ministry of Railways reply, PIB 19 March 2025: 2,741 of 2,843 route-km on the Eastern and Western Dedicated Freight Corridors was commissioned and operational (96.4%).

indicators.title: Latest Railway Freight Loading
indicators.subtitle: Year Book revenue-earning basis
indicators.details:
What it shows — Revenue-earning freight tonnes originating in the last two Year Book years.

How to read it — Loading rose from 1,509.10 to 1,588.06 million tonnes.

Why it matters — The short view makes the latest annual change easier to read.

series.note: Railway Board Year Book 2023-24, Freight Operation Table I: latest two annual revenue-earning freight loading figures.

indicators.title: Rail Freight Transport Work
indicators.subtitle: Goods transported by railway
indicators.details:
What it shows — Goods moved by rail, measured in million metric tonnes times kilometres.

How to read it — The series runs from 249,564.000 in 1995 to 719,762.000 in 2021.

Why it matters — This independent World Bank series provides a cross-mode data point.

series.note: World Bank indicator IS.RRS.GOOD.MT.K6; annual observations may lag the latest reporting year.

indicators.title: Cargo Handled at Major Ports
indicators.subtitle: 12 major ports, annual cargo throughput
indicators.details:
What it shows — Annual cargo throughput at India's 12 major ports.

How to read it — Major-port cargo reached 819.23 million tonnes in 2023-24, up from 784.31 million tonnes in 2022-23.

Why it matters — Ports handle international and coastal cargo at India's maritime gateways.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW Annual Report 2023-24, section 2.12: annual cargo throughput at the 12 major ports.

indicators.title: Major-Port Container Throughput
indicators.subtitle: Container traffic in million TEU
indicators.details:
What it shows — Twenty-foot equivalent units handled by the 12 major ports.

How to read it — Container throughput rose from 11.45 million TEU in 2022-23 to 12.31 million TEU in 2023-24.

Why it matters — TEUs measure containerised freight separately from bulk cargo tonnes.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW Annual Report 2023-24, section 2.12: major-port container traffic (the table reports TEUs in parentheses).

indicators.title: Major-Port Cargo by Commodity
indicators.subtitle: FY 2023-24, 12 major ports
indicators.details:
What it shows — Major-port cargo in the six commodity groups reported by the Ministry.

How to read it — POL was the largest reported group at 245.99 million tonnes; containers were 181.57 million tonnes.

Why it matters — The breakdown distinguishes liquid and dry bulk from containerised cargo.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW Annual Report 2023-24, section 2.12: commodity-wise cargo traffic at major ports, FY 2023-24.

indicators.title: Overseas and Coastal Port Traffic
indicators.subtitle: All major and non-major ports
indicators.details:
What it shows — Overseas, coastal and total cargo handled by all Indian ports.

How to read it — Provisional 2023-24 total was 1,542.415 million tonnes, including 332.740 million coastal tonnes.

Why it matters — The split avoids treating all port throughput as international freight.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW, Update on Indian Port Sector as at 31 March 2024, Table 1(b): overseas and coastal traffic at major and non-major ports combined. Converted from '000 tonnes; 2023-24 provisional. Rounded components may differ from total by 0.001.

indicators.title: Major vs Non-Major Port Cargo
indicators.subtitle: Port traffic by administrative class
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cargo traffic at major ports, non-major ports and all ports.

How to read it — The provisional 2023-24 update reports 819.004 million tonnes at major ports and 723.411 million tonnes at non-major ports.

Why it matters — Non-major ports carry a substantial share of Indian port traffic.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW, Update on Indian Port Sector as at 31 March 2024, Table 1(b): major, non-major and all-port traffic, converted from '000 tonnes. Provisional major-port value 819.004 differs from the annual report's later revised 819.23 MMT; revisions are not combined.

indicators.title: Major-Port Traffic: Reported Extremes
indicators.subtitle: Lowest and highest port totals
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cargo handled by the lowest- and highest-throughput major ports in the 2023-24 table.

How to read it — Paradip handled 145.38 million tonnes, while SMP Kolkata handled 16.63 million tonnes.

Why it matters — Port-level variation shows why the national total can conceal concentrated throughput.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW, Update on Indian Port Sector as at 31 March 2024: provisional 2023-24 cargo by major port; SMP Kolkata (16.63 MMT) and Paradip (145.38 MMT) were lowest and highest respectively.

indicators.title: Major-Port Cargo: Latest Annual Change
indicators.subtitle: Revised major-port totals
indicators.details:
What it shows — The two latest annual totals for the 12 major ports.

How to read it — Cargo increased from 784.31 to 819.23 million tonnes.

Why it matters — A short comparison highlights the latest annual change.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW Annual Report 2023-24, section 2.11: revised 12 major-port traffic for 2022-23 and 2023-24.

indicators.title: Air Cargo: Domestic and International
indicators.subtitle: Freight handled at all Indian airports
indicators.details:
What it shows — Air freight handled at Indian airports, in thousands of metric tonnes.

How to read it — Total was 3,365.68 thousand tonnes in 2023-24: 1,320.16 domestic and 2,045.52 international.

Why it matters — This airport-handled cargo measure differs from airline tonne-kilometres.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: AAI Annual Report 2023-24, Board's Report traffic table: freight handled at all Indian airports, domestic/international. This airport-handled basis differs from airline tonne-kilometres.

indicators.title: Air Freight: Domestic vs International
indicators.subtitle: Share of 3,365.68 thousand tonnes
indicators.details:
What it shows — Domestic and international share of air freight handled at Indian airports in FY 2023-24.

How to read it — International freight was 2,045.52 thousand tonnes; domestic freight was 1,320.16 thousand tonnes.

Why it matters — The split shows the relative scale of cross-border and domestic airport cargo.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: AAI Annual Report 2023-24, Board's Report traffic table: FY 2023-24 freight at all Indian airports.

indicators.title: National Air Cargo Growth
indicators.subtitle: Ministry-reported total air cargo
indicators.details:
What it shows — Ministry-reported national air cargo volume at two endpoints.

How to read it — Reported volume rose from 2.53 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 3.72 million tonnes in 2024-25.

Why it matters — The longer national series provides context beyond AAI's airport traffic table.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: Ministry of Civil Aviation, Our Performance page, Supporting Passenger and Cargo Movement: national air-cargo figure 2.53 Mt in 2014-15 and 3.72 Mt in 2024-25. This differs in basis from AAI's airport-handled FY 2023-24 table.

indicators.title: Freight Modal Split: NITI Aayog 2021
indicators.subtitle: Reported road/rail shares; other modes are residual
indicators.details:
What it shows — NITI Aayog's reported road and rail shares, with an arithmetic residual for unlisted modes.

How to read it — Reported road and rail shares are 71% and 18%; the residual to 100% is 11%.

Why it matters — A single labelled base avoids mixing road/rail estimates with later waterway figures.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW reply published 28 March 2025 quotes NITI Aayog's 2021 Fast Tracking Freight in India: road 71%, rail 18%. Other modes (11%) is the arithmetic residual to 100%, not an independently reported estimate.

indicators.title: Inland Waterway Freight Share
indicators.subtitle: Approximate current share in the 2025 reply
indicators.details:
What it shows — Reported approximate inland-waterway share plus calculated remainder.

How to read it — The Ministry reports inland water transport at approximately 2% of freight traffic.

Why it matters — The official reply identifies IWT's share separately from the NITI 2021 road/rail basis.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW reply, 28 March 2025: current inland water transport freight share is approximately 2%. The 98% remainder is a calculated complement, not a separate modal estimate.

indicators.title: India Logistics Performance Index Rank
indicators.subtitle: World Bank overall rank
indicators.details:
What it shows — India's overall rank in each reported World Bank LPI edition.

How to read it — India ranked 38th in 2023, compared with 44th in 2018.

Why it matters — The LPI captures logistics service and infrastructure perceptions across six dimensions.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: World Bank Logistics Performance Index DataBank, India overall rank series. LPI ranks are perception-based international benchmarking, not physical freight quantities.

indicators.title: Logistics Costs: Published Denominator Comparison
indicators.subtitle: NCAER estimate, FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — Same estimated logistics-cost numerator relative to GDP and non-services output.

How to read it — The estimate is 7.97% of GDP or 9.09% of non-services output; these are two denominator views, not years.

Why it matters — Explicit denominator labels avoid perpetuating unverified 13-14% GDP estimates.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: DPIIT / NCAER Report on Logistics Cost Assessment in India (2025): logistics cost was estimated at 7.97% of GDP and 9.09% of non-services output in FY 2023-24. Denominators differ and are labelled.

indicators.title: LEADS 2023 Survey Reach
indicators.subtitle: Responses and stakeholder consultations
indicators.details:
What it shows — Counts of survey responses and stakeholder consultations reported in LEADS 2023.

How to read it — The report records 7,321 responses across 36 States/UTs and more than 750 consultations.

Why it matters — Sample size gives context for the state-level logistics assessment.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: DPIIT LEADS 2023: 7,321 responses across 36 States/UTs and more than 750 stakeholder consultations. Chart uses 750 as a minimum count for 'more than 750'.

indicators.title: LEADS 2023 Coverage
indicators.subtitle: LEADS 2023
indicators.details:
What it shows — Number of States and Union Territories covered.

How to read it — LEADS 2023 reports responses from all 36 States and Union Territories.

Why it matters — Coverage contextualises the national state-level comparison.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: DPIIT LEADS 2023: 7,321 survey responses were received across 36 States and Union Territories.

indicators.title: National Waterway Cargo Movement
indicators.subtitle: Inland water freight, not sea-port cargo
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cargo moved on India's National Waterways at the two reported endpoints.

How to read it — Cargo movement rose from 18.10 to 133.03 million tonnes.

Why it matters — The inland-water series adds a distinct water mode to the logistics comparison.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW reply, PIB 10 December 2024: cargo moved on National Waterways rose from 18.10 Mt in 2013-14 to 133.03 Mt in 2023-24. Inland waterways are not seaport cargo.

indicators.title: Indian Railways Earnings Mix
indicators.subtitle: Passenger and freight earnings, FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — Passenger-service and freight-service earnings of Indian Railways.

How to read it — Freight earnings were Rs 1,65,880.58 crore versus Rs 70,693.32 crore from passenger services.

Why it matters — The split shows the financial weight of freight on rail operations.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: Railway Board Year Book 2023-24, Passenger Business and Freight Operation earnings for FY 2023-24; freight excludes demurrage and wharfage.

indicators.title: Railway Freight and Passenger Earnings
indicators.subtitle: Earnings by service
indicators.details:
What it shows — Indian Railways earnings from passenger and freight services.

How to read it — FY 2023-24 freight earnings were Rs 1,65,880.58 crore, versus passenger earnings of Rs 70,693.32 crore.

Why it matters — The comparison shows the financial weight of freight on the railway system.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: Railway Board Year Book 2023-24, Passenger Business and Freight Operation earnings; freight excludes demurrage and wharfage.

indicators.title: Rail Passenger and Freight Yield
indicators.subtitle: Revenue per traffic unit
indicators.details:
What it shows — Passenger earnings per passenger-km and freight earnings per net tonne-km.

How to read it — Freight yield was 170.31 paise per NTKM in 2023-24; passenger yield was 66.40 paise per passenger-km.

Why it matters — Different traffic bases are explicitly named for comparison.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: Railway Board Year Book 2023-24, Selected Financial Ratios: earnings/yield ratios based on apportioned earnings.

indicators.title: FASTag Toll Collections
indicators.subtitle: FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — Approximate toll fees collected through FASTag.

How to read it — Around Rs 55,000 crore was collected through FASTag in FY 2023-24.

Why it matters — Toll-user-fee collection is not freight-operator revenue.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: NHAI Annual Report 2023-24, citing IHMCL: FASTag collection was around Rs 55,000 crore in FY 2023-24.

indicators.title: NHAI Toll-Operate-Transfer Proceeds
indicators.subtitle: FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — Asset monetisation, FY 2023-24

How to read it — NHAI realised Rs 15,968 crore from four TOT bundles.

Why it matters — Asset monetisation is shown separately from recurring toll receipts.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoRTH Year End Review 2024: NHAI monetised four Toll-Operate-Transfer bundles, realising Rs 15,968 crore in FY 2023-24. These asset proceeds are not recurring toll collections.

indicators.title: Railway Freight Earnings over Five Years
indicators.details:
What it shows — Cumulative goods earnings

How to read it — The Ministry reported Rs 7,02,372.29 crore in goods earnings during 2019-2024.

Why it matters — The multiyear total provides a separate scale reference from annual earnings.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

datasets.label: Railway Freight Earnings over Five Years

series.note: Ministry of Railways Lok Sabha reply / PIB, March 2025: cumulative goods earnings reported for the five-year period 2019-2024.

indicators.title: Estimated National Logistics Cost
indicators.subtitle: Current-price estimate, FY 2023-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — NCAER's estimated aggregate logistics cost at current prices.

How to read it — The report estimates Rs 24.01 lakh crore, equal to 7.97% of GDP in FY 2023-24.

Why it matters — Distinguishes a documented cost estimate from unsupported market-size claims.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: DPIIT / NCAER Report on Logistics Cost Assessment in India (2025): total logistics cost estimated at Rs 24.01 lakh crore at current prices for FY 2023-24. This is cost, not revenue or market size.

indicators.title: Major-Port Commodity Traffic: Annual Comparison
indicators.subtitle: 12 major ports
indicators.details:
What it shows — Major-port cargo by the published commodity groups for the two latest years.

How to read it — POL rose from 234.17 to 245.99 million tonnes; iron ore increased from 46.51 to 61.03 million tonnes.

Why it matters — Year comparison shows which commodities account for changes in port throughput.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: MoPSW Annual Report 2023-24, section 2.12: major-port commodity totals, FY 2022-23 and FY 2023-24.

indicators.title: Airport-Handled Air Cargo Growth
indicators.subtitle: All Indian airports
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total freight handled at all Indian airports in AAI's reported years.

How to read it — Handled freight rose from 3,146.80 to 3,365.68 thousand tonnes.

Why it matters — This airport-handled measure complements the national MoCA series.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: AAI Annual Report 2023-24, Board's Report traffic table: total freight handled at all Indian airports, domestic plus international.

indicators.title: World Bank Container Port Traffic
indicators.subtitle: Container port traffic
indicators.details:
What it shows — Container port traffic measured in twenty-foot equivalent units.

How to read it — The series runs from 9,235,765.000 in 2010 to 23,898,000.000 in 2024.

Why it matters — This country series complements the Ministry's major-port container figures.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: World Bank indicator IS.SHP.GOOD.TU; annual observations may lag the latest reporting year.

indicators.title: Air Freight: India and Peers
indicators.subtitle: Freight transported by registered carriers
indicators.details:
What it shows — Air freight in tonne-kilometres reported to the World Bank/ICAO.

How to read it — India is shown with selected peer economies; missing reports are gaps, not zeros.

Why it matters — Tonne-kilometres add distance moved to cargo weight.
indicators.subgroup: Sea & Air Freight, Modal Split & Revenue

series.note: World Bank indicator IS.AIR.GOOD.MT.K1, compiled from national statistical sources (air freight uses ICAO data). Missing years/countries are gaps, not zeros.

indicators.title: Current Health Expenditure
indicators.subtitle: Current health expenditure as a share of GDP
indicators.details: Current health expenditure relative to GDP. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Physicians per 1,000 People
indicators.subtitle: Medical doctors per 1,000 people
indicators.details: Practising physicians per 1,000 people. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Basic Drinking Water Access
indicators.subtitle: Population using at least basic drinking water services
indicators.details: Population using at least basic drinking-water services. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Basic Sanitation Access
indicators.subtitle: Population using at least basic sanitation services
indicators.details: Population using at least basic sanitation services. Sourced from World Bank Open Data.

indicators.title: Government Health Spending per Capita
indicators.subtitle: Domestic general government health expenditure per person in current US dollars
indicators.details: Domestic general government health expenditure per capita in current US dollars. Nominal values are not adjusted for inflation.

indicators.title: Safely Managed Drinking Water
indicators.subtitle: Population using safely managed drinking-water services
indicators.details: Share of the population using safely managed drinking-water services, as estimated in the World Bank series.

indicators.title: Tuberculosis Incidence
indicators.subtitle: New and relapse TB cases per 100,000 people
indicators.details: New and relapse TB cases per 100,000 people. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.TBS.INCD); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: New and relapse TB cases per 100,000 people. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.TBS.INCD); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Hospital Beds
indicators.subtitle: Hospital beds per 1,000 people
indicators.details: Hospital beds per 1,000 people. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.MED.BEDS.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: Hospital beds per 1,000 people. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.MED.BEDS.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: DPT Immunization
indicators.subtitle: Children aged 12-23 months immunized against DPT
indicators.details: Children aged 12-23 months immunized against DPT. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.IMM.IDPT); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: Children aged 12-23 months immunized against DPT. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.IMM.IDPT); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Smoking Prevalence
indicators.subtitle: Adults who smoke (WHO age-standardised)
indicators.details: Adults who smoke (WHO age-standardised). Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.PRV.SMOK); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: Adults who smoke (WHO age-standardised). Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.PRV.SMOK); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Malaria Incidence
indicators.subtitle: Malaria cases per 1,000 people at risk
indicators.details: Malaria cases per 1,000 people at risk. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.MLR.INCD.P3); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: Malaria cases per 1,000 people at risk. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.MLR.INCD.P3); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Health in Government Expenditure
indicators.subtitle: Domestic general government health expenditure as a share of total government spending
indicators.details: Domestic general government health expenditure as a share of total government spending. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.XPD.GHED.GE.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

series.note: Domestic general government health expenditure as a share of total government spending. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.XPD.GHED.GE.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Prevalence of Undernourishment
indicators.subtitle: Share of population below minimum calorie needs, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — The FAO estimate of the share of Indians whose usual food intake does not meet minimum energy needs.

How to read it — Lower is better. It is a three-year average, so it moves slowly.

Why it matters — Hunger is SDG 2 and the target of the National Food Security Act and PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana; this is also an input to the Global Hunger Index.

series.note: Share of population below minimum calorie needs, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SN.ITK.DEFC.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Child Stunting (modelled)
indicators.subtitle: Children under 5 too short for their age, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of children under five who are too short for their age, a sign of chronic undernutrition.

How to read it — Lower is better; the trend comes from UNICEF/WHO/World Bank modelled estimates that smooth survey years (NFHS).

Why it matters — Stunting harms brain development and lifetime earnings and is the main target of POSHAN Abhiyaan.

series.note: Children under 5 too short for their age, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.STA.STNT.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Measles Immunisation
indicators.subtitle: Children aged 12-23 months vaccinated, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of young children who have received the measles vaccine.

How to read it — Higher is better; at least 95% is needed to stop measles outbreaks. Dips show disruptions such as COVID-19.

Why it matters — Measles coverage is a bellwether for the whole routine-immunisation system under Mission Indradhanush.

series.note: Children aged 12-23 months vaccinated, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SH.IMM.MEAS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Who Pays for Health Care (2023)
indicators.subtitle: Share of current health expenditure
indicators.details: Share of current health expenditure, latest year with every component reported (2023). World Bank indicators SH.XPD.GHED.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.PVTD.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.EHEX.CH.ZS.

series.note: Share of current health expenditure, latest year with every component reported (2023). World Bank indicators SH.XPD.GHED.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.PVTD.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.EHEX.CH.ZS.
series.source: World Bank API SH.XPD.GHED.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.PVTD.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.EHEX.CH.ZS

indicators.title: Causes of Death (2021)
indicators.subtitle: Share of total deaths (WHO)
indicators.details: Share of total deaths (WHO), latest year with every component reported (2021). World Bank indicators SH.DTH.COMM.ZS, SH.DTH.NCOM.ZS, SH.DTH.INJR.ZS.

series.note: Share of total deaths (WHO), latest year with every component reported (2021). World Bank indicators SH.DTH.COMM.ZS, SH.DTH.NCOM.ZS, SH.DTH.INJR.ZS.
series.source: World Bank API SH.DTH.COMM.ZS, SH.DTH.NCOM.ZS, SH.DTH.INJR.ZS

indicators.title: Out-of-Pocket vs Government Health Spending (2023)
indicators.subtitle: Share of current health expenditure
indicators.details: Share of current health expenditure, latest year with every component reported (2023). World Bank indicators SH.XPD.OOPC.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.GHED.CH.ZS. 'Other prepaid private & external' is the residual to 100%, not a directly reported category.

series.note: Share of current health expenditure, latest year with every component reported (2023). World Bank indicators SH.XPD.OOPC.CH.ZS, SH.XPD.GHED.CH.ZS. 'Other prepaid private & external' is the residual to 100%, not a directly reported category.

indicators.title: Malaria Cases (NCVBDC)
indicators.subtitle: Reported cases nationwide
indicators.details:
What it shows — Malaria cases reported through the National Centre for Vector Borne Diseases Control, with the more dangerous P. falciparum cases shown separately.

How to read it — Falling lines mean fewer infections; India's caseload has dropped by more than 80% since 2015.

Why it matters — India aims to eliminate malaria by 2030, so steady declines, especially in falciparum cases, track progress toward that goal.

series.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 119 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Values for 2023, 2024 are marked provisional by the source. National totals are the sum of State/UT reports; the most recent years are provisional.

indicators.title: Dengue Cases (NCVBDC)
indicators.subtitle: Reported cases nationwide
indicators.details:
What it shows — Laboratory-reported dengue cases in India each year.

How to read it — Bars swing with monsoon conditions and urban mosquito breeding; the long-run trend is upward, partly because testing has improved.

Why it matters — Dengue is an expanding urban health threat linked to water storage, construction and a warming climate, with no widely used vaccine yet.

series.note: Source: MoSPI EnviStats India, indicator 120 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Values for 2023 are marked provisional by the source. National totals are the sum of State/UT reports; the most recent years are provisional.

indicators.title: Infant Mortality Rate by Sex (SRS)
indicators.subtitle: Deaths before age one per 1,000 live births
indicators.details:
What it shows — Out of every 1,000 babies born alive, how many die before their first birthday, from the Registrar General's Sample Registration System.

How to read it — All lines falling means more infants survive. Girls' mortality was once higher than boys', which is unusual biologically; watch whether that gap has closed.

Why it matters — Infant mortality is a summary of maternal health, nutrition, immunisation and sanitation; SDG 3 asks India to keep pushing it down.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 15 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Under-Five Mortality Rate by Sex (SRS)
indicators.subtitle: Deaths before age five per 1,000 live births
indicators.details:
What it shows — Deaths of children before their fifth birthday per 1,000 live births, from the Sample Registration System.

How to read it — Lower is better; the SDG target is 25 or fewer by 2030. Compare girls with boys for signs of gender bias in child care.

Why it matters — Under-five deaths are mostly preventable (pneumonia, diarrhoea, newborn complications), so this measures how well basic health services reach children.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 17 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Life Expectancy at Birth by Sex (SRS)
indicators.subtitle: Years, five-year moving periods
indicators.details:
What it shows — How many years a newborn would live on average if current death rates held, from SRS abridged life tables for overlapping five-year periods.

How to read it — Both lines rising means longer lives. Women overtook men in the 1990s and the gap has widened, the normal pattern as health care improves.

Why it matters — Life expectancy sums up a country's health in one number and shapes pension, health and elder-care planning.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 18 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Projected periods (2021-25 onward) published alongside the estimates are excluded.

indicators.title: Maternal Mortality Ratio (SRS)
indicators.subtitle: Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births
indicators.details:
What it shows — Women who die from pregnancy or childbirth complications per 100,000 live births, from SRS special bulletins on maternal mortality.

How to read it — Each bar is a pooled period (for example 2018-20). India has passed its National Health Policy target of 100 and is heading toward the SDG goal of 70.

Why it matters — The fall reflects institutional deliveries under Janani Suraksha Yojana and better emergency obstetric care, and shows what is left to do.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 21 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Maternal Mortality Ratio by State (SRS) (2021-23)
indicators.subtitle: Maternal deaths per 100,000 live births
indicators.details:
What it shows — The maternal mortality ratio in each larger State for the latest SRS period.

How to read it — Longer bars are worse. Assam, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh usually rank highest; Kerala, Maharashtra and Telangana lowest.

Why it matters — The spread between States shows that national progress hides large regional gaps where maternal-health spending is most needed.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 21 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2021-23. Ranked highest to lowest.

indicators.title: Tuberculosis Mortality
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Estimated tuberculosis deaths per 100,000 people (HIV-negative). This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 21 per 100,000 in 2024. Falling lines show progress toward TB elimination targets.

Why it matters — India carries the world's largest TB burden, so mortality progress is globally significant.

series.note: Tuberculosis Mortality: India's annual series, 2000 to 2024; the latest value is 21 per 100,000. Source: World Bank API SH.TBS.MORT (WHO Global TB / Malaria Programmes via World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

Why it matters — India carries the world's largest TB burden, so mortality progress is globally significant.

indicators.title: TB Case Detection Rate
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2024
indicators.details:
What it shows — Estimated share of new and relapse TB cases that were detected and reported. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 92% in 2024. Higher means fewer hidden cases; 100% means all cases are notified.

Why it matters — Detection is the gateway to treatment and to stopping transmission.

series.note: TB Case Detection Rate: India's annual series, 2000 to 2024; the latest value is 92%. Source: World Bank API SH.TBS.DTEC.ZS (WHO Global TB / Malaria Programmes via World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: TB Treatment Success Rate
indicators.subtitle: India, 2000-2023
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of TB cases successfully treated (cured or treatment completed). This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 90% in 2023. Higher is better; dips show drop-outs or drug resistance.

Why it matters — Treatment success determines whether TB is actually eliminated.

series.note: TB Treatment Success Rate: India's annual series, 2000 to 2023; the latest value is 90%. Source: World Bank API SH.TBS.CURE.ZS (WHO Global TB / Malaria Programmes via World Bank); latest year with data: 2023.

How to read it — India is the orange line; the others are China, United States, Japan, Germany, Brazil, Bangladesh. Higher is better; dips show drop-outs or drug resistance.

Why it matters — Treatment success determines whether TB is actually eliminated.

series.note: TB Treatment Success Rate: India against 6 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API SH.TBS.CURE.ZS (WHO Global TB / Malaria Programmes via World Bank); latest year with data: 2023.

indicators.subtitle: India against major economies and neighbours

Why it matters — Malaria incidence tracks the success of vector control and diagnosis.

series.note: Malaria Incidence: India against 3 comparison countries; gaps are years without a reported value. Source: World Bank API SH.MLR.INCD.P3 (WHO Global TB / Malaria Programmes via World Bank); latest year with data: 2024.

indicators.title: NITI Health Index: overall score by state and UT
indicators.subtitle: Overall reference-year (2019-20) Health Index score out of 100
indicators.details:
What it shows — The composite Health Index score for every state and UT in Round IV (reference year 2019-20), combining health outcomes, governance and information, and key inputs and processes.

How to read it — A longer bar means a better composite score. Kerala leads the larger states and Mizoram the smaller ones; Uttar Pradesh and Bihar are lowest among the larger states.

indicators.title: Population
indicators.subtitle: Total population
indicators.details:
Population provides the denominator and demographic context for many other indicators. A growing population can expand the workforce and consumer base while also increasing demand for jobs, housing, health, and infrastructure.

This is a count of people, not a welfare measure. Per-capita indicators and age structure are needed to understand how demographic change affects living standards.

indicators.title: Unemployment rate
indicators.subtitle: Share of the labour force without work
indicators.details:
The unemployment rate measures the share of the labour force that is without work but available for and seeking employment. It does not capture underemployment or people who have stopped looking for work.

Labour-market comparisons require care because survey design and informal employment affect measurement. This annual series is a useful macro context signal rather than a complete employment dashboard.

indicators.title: Electricity access
indicators.subtitle: Population with access to electricity
indicators.details:
Electricity access measures the share of the population with access to electricity. It is a core infrastructure and living-conditions indicator with direct relevance to households, schools, businesses, and digital services.

Coverage does not fully describe reliability, affordability, or quality of supply. The series is annual and sourced through the open World Bank API.

indicators.title: Internet users
indicators.subtitle: Individuals using the internet
indicators.details:
Internet use measures the share of people using the internet. It provides a broad signal of digital access and the potential reach of online services, payments, education, and commerce.

The metric does not measure connection speed, affordability, quality, or intensity of use. Those dimensions require more detailed telecom and household datasets.

indicators.title: Life expectancy
indicators.subtitle: Life expectancy at birth
indicators.details:
Life expectancy at birth estimates the average years a newborn would live under current mortality conditions. It is a high-level outcome indicator for population health and social development.

It is not an individual prediction and does not reveal regional, gender, or income differences. Trends should be interpreted alongside health-system and demographic data.

indicators.title: Youth Unemployment (ILO estimate)
indicators.subtitle: Unemployed as % of labour force aged 15-24
indicators.details:
What it shows — The ILO-modelled unemployment rate for young people aged 15-24, comparable across countries.

How to read it — Read it with the PLFS youth chart: the methods differ, but both show youth unemployment far above the overall rate.

Why it matters — It shows how well the economy absorbs new entrants into the workforce each year.

series.note: Unemployed as % of labour force aged 15-24. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SL.UEM.1524.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Labour Force Participation Rate (PLFS)
indicators.subtitle: Share of people aged 15+ working or seeking work
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of people aged 15 and over who are in the labour force (working or looking for work), from the Periodic Labour Force Survey.

How to read it — Compare the women's line with the men's: the gap shows how many women are outside paid work. A rising women's line is the biggest labour-market change since 2017-18.

Why it matters — Participation, not just unemployment, decides how much of India's demographic dividend turns into output and household income.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 1 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

indicators.title: Worker Population Ratio (PLFS)
indicators.subtitle: Share of people aged 15+ who are employed
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of the population aged 15 and over that is actually employed.

How to read it — This is the employment rate: it rises when jobs grow faster than population. Read it alongside the participation chart.

Why it matters — It is the most direct measure of how many people the economy employs, and it includes self-employment and unpaid family work.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 2 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

indicators.title: Unemployment Rate (PLFS)
indicators.subtitle: Share of the labour force aged 15+ without work
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of people in the labour force (aged 15+) who looked for work but found none.

How to read it — Lower is better. A falling line together with a rising participation rate is a genuinely tightening labour market.

Why it matters — This is India's official headline unemployment measure, used for policy and to compare States.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

indicators.title: Youth Unemployment Rate, 15-29 (PLFS)
indicators.subtitle: Share of the labour force aged 15-29 without work
indicators.details:
What it shows — The unemployment rate among young people aged 15-29.

How to read it — Youth unemployment runs well above the overall rate; watch the gap between young women and young men.

Why it matters — Joblessness among educated young people is a key political and economic issue and the target of skilling and apprenticeship schemes.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Periodic Labour Force Survey, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Usual status (principal + subsidiary), rural + urban, agricultural years July-June.

indicators.title: Out-of-School Children of Primary Age
indicators.subtitle: India, 1990-2025
indicators.details:
What it shows — Share of primary-school-age children who are not enrolled in school. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 0.12% in 2025. Lower is better; spikes show enrolment shocks.

Why it matters — Out-of-school children are the clearest measure of unfinished universal education.

series.note: Out-of-School Children of Primary Age: India's annual series, 1990 to 2025; the latest value is 0.12%. Source: World Bank API SE.PRM.UNER.ZS (UNESCO UIS / ILO / UNICEF via World Bank); latest year with data: 2025.

indicators.details:
What it shows — Gross enrolment in pre-primary education. This chart follows India's annual series.

How to read it — The line ends at 51.69% gross in 2021. Higher means more children start learning before primary school.

Why it matters — Early education raises later learning outcomes and lets mothers work.

Why it matters — Early education raises later learning outcomes and lets mothers work.

How to read it — Bars are the headcount ratio in percent. Bihar, Jharkhand and Meghalaya are highest; Kerala, Goa and Puducherry are lowest.

indicators.title: Research & Development Spending
indicators.subtitle: Gross domestic spending on R&D, % of GDP
indicators.details:
What it shows — Total spending on research and development by government, business and universities as a share of GDP.

How to read it — India's figure stays near 0.7%, against about 2.5% in China and over 3% in the US and South Korea.

Why it matters — R&D drives innovation and productivity; the Anusandhan National Research Foundation is meant to lift private research spending.

series.note: Gross domestic spending on R&D, % of GDP. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator GB.XPD.RSDV.GD.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Researchers per Million People
indicators.subtitle: Full-time researchers in R&D per million population
indicators.details:
What it shows — The number of people working full-time in research per million population.

How to read it — Higher means a larger research workforce; India's figure is low by international standards.

Why it matters — A country's research base decides its ability to innovate in fields from vaccines to semiconductors.

series.note: Full-time researchers in R&D per million population. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SP.POP.SCIE.RD.P6); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Literacy Rate by Sex (age 7+)
indicators.subtitle: Census 1981-2011 and NSS 2017-18, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of people aged seven and over who can read and write, from the Census and the NSS 75th round (2017-18).

How to read it — The gap between men's and women's lines is the gender literacy gap; it has narrowed steadily since 1981.

Why it matters — Literacy is the base for employability, health awareness and civic participation, and women's literacy in particular predicts child health.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 55 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Gross Enrolment Ratio by Stage (UDISE+/AISHE)
indicators.subtitle: Enrolment as % of the official age group
indicators.details:
What it shows — Enrolment at each stage of education as a percentage of the population of the matching age group.

How to read it — Primary is near or above 100% (universal), but each later stage is lower: the drop between lines shows where children leave school.

Why it matters — The National Education Policy targets 100% GER up to secondary level and 50% in higher education by 2035.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 60 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: School Dropout Rate by Stage (UDISE+)
indicators.subtitle: Average annual dropout rate, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of students who leave school during the year at each stage, from UDISE+.

How to read it — Lower is better. Secondary-stage dropout is several times higher than primary, which is where most children are lost.

Why it matters — Dropout shows whether rising enrolment turns into completed schooling; secondary dropout is the main focus of Samagra Shiksha.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 74 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Number of Universities (AISHE)
indicators.subtitle: Universities and university-level institutions
indicators.details:
What it shows — The number of universities in India in each All India Survey on Higher Education.

How to read it — Each bar is an academic year; steady growth means new central, State, private and deemed universities opening.

Why it matters — More institutions widen access, but the quality of what is taught matters as much as the count.

series.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 1 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Number of Colleges (AISHE)
indicators.subtitle: Colleges affiliated to universities
indicators.details:
What it shows — The number of colleges in India in each AISHE round.

How to read it — Bars rising year on year show expansion; most new colleges are private and small.

Why it matters — Colleges teach the bulk of India's undergraduates, so their spread decides how many students can get a degree near home.

series.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 2 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Higher Education Enrolment by Sex (AISHE)
indicators.subtitle: Estimated students enrolled
indicators.details:
What it shows — The estimated number of students enrolled in higher education, split by sex.

How to read it — Women's enrolment has nearly caught up with men's; where the lines cross, women outnumber men.

Why it matters — Higher-education enrolment builds the skilled workforce, and women's rising share is one of India's quieter social shifts.

series.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Higher Education Enrolment by Level (AISHE) (2021-22)
indicators.subtitle: Share of students by programme level
indicators.details:
What it shows — How students in higher education are spread across programme levels in the latest AISHE round.

How to read it — Undergraduates are the overwhelming majority; Ph.D. students are a sliver, which is relevant to India's research capacity.

Why it matters — The mix shows whether the system mostly produces first degrees or advanced skills and research.

series.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 3 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2021-22.

indicators.title: Higher Education GER by Social Group (AISHE)
indicators.subtitle: Gross enrolment ratio, age 18-23, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — Higher-education enrolment as a share of the 18-23 age group for all students, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

How to read it — The gap between the 'All' line and the SC and ST lines measures unequal access; narrowing gaps mean more inclusive growth.

Why it matters — GER is the headline access measure under NEP 2020 (target 50% by 2035), and group gaps guide scholarships and reservation policy.

series.note: Source: Ministry of Education AISHE via MoSPI, indicator 6 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.subtitle: Gross enrolment ratio, age 18-23, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — The higher-education gross enrolment ratio in each State and UT for the latest AISHE round.

How to read it — Longer bars mean more young people in college. Southern States and some UTs lead; large northern and eastern States trail.

Why it matters — State gaps show where new colleges, scholarships and hostels would do the most to raise national enrolment.

labels: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu

How to read it — Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Chandigarh lead; Jharkhand and Bihar are at the bottom of the large states.

Why it matters — Gives states an outcome-focused benchmark for school education policy.

indicators.details:

How to read it — Haryana, Assam and Puducherry improved most; Karnataka, Uttarakhand, Mizoram and Sikkim slipped.

Why it matters — Separates states that are improving quickly from those that merely start high.

indicators.details:

indicators.subtitle: Share of Lok Sabha seats held by women, %
indicators.details:
What it shows — The share of seats in the lower house of Parliament held by women.

How to read it — Steps in the line follow general elections. The Women's Reservation Act (2023) will reserve one-third of seats once it takes effect.

Why it matters — Representation shapes which issues reach the legislative agenda.

series.note: Share of Lok Sabha seats held by women, %. Official national statistics compiled by the World Bank (indicator SG.GEN.PARL.ZS); gaps reflect years without a reported value.

indicators.title: Sex Ratio at Birth (SRS)
indicators.subtitle: Girls born per 1,000 boys, three-year periods
indicators.details:
What it shows — How many girls are born for every 1,000 boys, from the Sample Registration System.

How to read it — The natural ratio is about 950. Values well below that point to sex-selective abortion; an upward trend means the gap is closing.

Why it matters — This is the key outcome for Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and the PC-PNDT Act, and it shapes future marriage markets and demography.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 7 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Population Sex Ratio (Census 1951-2011)
indicators.subtitle: Females per 1,000 males
indicators.details:
What it shows — Females per 1,000 males in the whole population at each Census from 1951 to 2011.

How to read it — A value below 1,000 means fewer women than men. India's ratio dipped to 927 in 1991 and recovered to 943 by 2011.

Why it matters — A persistently low sex ratio reflects excess female mortality and son preference; it is one of the starkest gender indicators.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 2 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.title: Women's Mean Age at Marriage (SRS)
indicators.subtitle: Average age at effective marriage, years
indicators.details:
What it shows — The average age at which women marry, from the Sample Registration System.

How to read it — Higher is better for health and education outcomes. Urban women marry about two years later than rural women.

Why it matters — Later marriage is linked to more schooling, lower fertility and better maternal and child health; it is also behind the debate on raising the legal age of marriage to 21.

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 14 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/).

indicators.details:
What it shows — The average number of children a woman would have over her life, grouped by her education level, for the latest SRS year.

How to read it — Bars fall from left to right: illiterate women have the most children and graduates the fewest.

Why it matters — Girls' education is one of the most powerful levers on population growth, maternal health and child welfare.

datasets.label: Total Fertility Rate by Women's Education (SRS) (2023)

series.note: Source: MoSPI Women & Men in India, indicator 10 on the MoSPI API platform (https://esankhyiki.mospi.gov.in/). Latest period reported: 2023.
